questions.q: An aeroplane flying with uniform speed horizontally one $\mathrm{km}$ above the ground is observed at an elevation of $60^{{}^{\circ}}$. After $10 \mathrm{ s}$ if the elevation is observed to be $30^{{}^{\circ}}$, then the speed of the plane (in $\mathrm{km} / \mathrm{h}$ ) is
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{llll} \\ \tan 60^{{}^{\circ}} & =\frac{D P}{A P} \\ \\ \Rightarrow \sqrt{3} & =\frac{1}{A P} \\ \\ \Rightarrow A P & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & {[\because E Q=D P=1]} \\ \end{array} \\ In \Delta$E A Q$, \\ \begin{aligned}$
\tan 30^{{}^{\circ}} & =$\frac{E Q}{A P+P Q}$\\
\Rightarrow $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$& =$\frac{1}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}+P Q} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}+$P Q=$\sqrt{3}$\\
\Rightarrow P Q & =$\sqrt{3}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \mathrm{~km}$\\
\therefore $\text{ Speed of plane }$& =$\frac{\text{ Distance }}{\text{ Time }}=\frac{2 / \sqrt{3}}{\frac{10}{60 \times 60}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \times \frac{3600}{10}$\\
& =240 $\sqrt{3} \mathrm{~km}$/ $\mathrm{h}$
\end{aligned}

questions.q: A tower subtends angles $\alpha, 2 \alpha$ and $3 \alpha$ respectively at points $A, B$ and $C$, all lying on a horizontal line through the foot of the tower, then $\frac{A B}{B C}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
In $\triangle E C D$, $\tan 3 \alpha=\frac{h}{C D}$
$\Rightarrow \quad C D=h \cot 3 \alpha \quad \ldots(\mathrm{i})$ In $\triangle E B D$, $\tan 2 \alpha=\frac{h}{B D}\Rightarrow \quad B D=h \cot 2 \alpha \quad \ldots(\mathrm{ii})$ In $\triangle E A D$, $\tan \alpha=\frac{h}{A D}\Rightarrow \quad A D=h \cot \alpha \quad \ldots(\mathrm{iii})$ From Eqs. (ii) and (iii), $A D-B D=h \cot \alpha-h \cot 2 \alphaA B=h(\cot \alpha-\cot 2 \alpha) \quad \ldots(\mathrm{iv})$ From Eqs. (i) and (ii), $B D-C D=h \cot 2 \alpha-h \cot 3 \alphaB C=h(\cot 2 \alpha-\cot 3 \alpha) \quad \ldots(\mathrm{v})$ From Eqs. (iv) and (v), $\frac{A B}{B C}=\frac{h(\cot \alpha-\cot 2 \alpha)}{2(\cot 2 \alpha-\cot 3 \alpha)}\Rightarrow \frac{A B}{B C}=\frac{\frac{\cos \alpha}{\sin \alpha}-\frac{\cos 2 \alpha}{\sin 2 \alpha}}{\frac{\cos 2 \alpha}{\sin 2 \alpha}-\frac{\cos 3 \alpha}{\sin 3 \alpha}}=\frac{\frac{\sin (2 \alpha-\alpha)}{\sin \alpha \sin 2 \alpha}}{\frac{\sin (3 \alpha-2 \alpha)}{\sin 2 \alpha \sin 3 \alpha}}=\frac{\sin 3 \alpha}{\sin \alpha}=\frac{3 \sin \alpha-4 \sin ^3 \alpha}{\sin \alpha}=3-4 \sin ^2 \alpha=-3-2(1-\cos 2 \alpha)=1+2 \cos 2 \alpha$

questions.solution:
Given equation of hyperbola
$5 x^2-k y^2=12\Rightarrow \frac{x^2}{\frac{12}{5}}-\frac{y^2}{\frac{12}{k}}=1$
So equation of tangent at $\left(x_1, y_1\right)$ is
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{x_1}{a^2} x-\frac{y_1}{b^2} y=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{x_1}{\frac{12}{5}} x-\frac{y_1}{\frac{12}{k}} y=1 \Rightarrow \frac{5 x_1}{12} x-\frac{k y_1}{12} y=1\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \frac{5 x_1}{2} x-\frac{k y_1}{2} y=6$
So, $\frac{5 x_1}{2}=5 \Rightarrow x_1=2, \frac{k y_1}{2}=2 \Rightarrow y_1=\frac{4}{k}\begin{aligned} & \text{ Now, } 5 \times 4-k \times \frac{16}{k^2}=12 \\ & \Rightarrow 20-12=\frac{16}{k} \Rightarrow k=2\end{aligned}$
Since, $(\sqrt{6}, p)$ satisfied the hyperbola
$\Rightarrow 5 \times 6-2 \times p^2=12 \Rightarrow p=-3, p < 0$
So, equation of normal at $(\sqrt{6},-3)$ is
$\frac{a^2}{x_1} x+\frac{b^2}{y_1} y=a^2+b^2\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{12}{5 \times \sqrt{6}} x+\frac{12}{2 \times(-3)} y=\frac{12}{5}+\frac{12}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{x}{5 \sqrt{6}}-\frac{y}{6}=\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \frac{\sqrt{6} x-5 y}{30}=\frac{7}{10} \Rightarrow \sqrt{6} x-5 y=21$

questions.q: If the line $a x+b y+c=0$ is a normal to the curve $x y=1$, then
questions.solution:
Given curve is $x y=1$
So, $y=\frac{1}{x}$ ...(i)
Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get,
$x \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}+y=0[\because(u v) \prime=u v \prime+u \prime v]\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}=-\frac{y}{x}$
Given line is, $a x+b y+c=0$
The slope of a line is the coefficient of $x$ in
$y=m x+c$ form.
Thus, the slope of the given line is, $-\frac{a}{b}$
Thus the slope of tangent is,
$\frac{b}{a}, \left[\because\right. slope of normal \left.=-\frac{1}{\text{ slope of line }}\right]
Since the slope is normal to the curve, the normal of the line will be tangent to the curve. Thus,
$-$\frac{y}{x}=\frac{b}{a}\Rightarrow-\frac{\frac{1}{x}}{x}=\frac{b}{a} \left[\becausey=\frac{1}{x}\right]
So, LHS will always be a positive value, so \frac{a}{b} in the RHS must be negative. For that to happen, $ a$ and $b$ must have the opposite signs.
Thus, $a > 0, b < 0$ or $a < 0, b > 0$.$

questions.q: If the normal to the rectangular hyperbola $x^{2} - y^{2} = 1$ at the point $P  \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) meets the curve again at $ Q $\left(\theta\right)$,$then \sec^{2}\theta ++tan\theta =$
questions.solution:
Given,

Equation of hyperbola& $x^{2} - y^{2} = 1$

Now parametric point is given by~$\left(a\text{sec}\theta, btan\theta\right) ≡ \left(\sqrt{2}, 1\right)~as given& $\theta = 45 ° & a = b = 1$

Now finding slope of tangent at the given point by differentiating the curve we get,

~$2x - 2y$\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$0$

$⇒ $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}$\right)$\left(\sqrt{2}, 1\right)$ = $\dfrac{2}{1}

So, slope of $normal will be~- \sqrt{2}$,

Now equation of normal will be~$y = $\dfrac{- x}{2} +$2$

Since normal is intersecting the curve again so,

$x^{2} - $\left(\dfrac{- x}{2} +2\right)$2 = 1$

$⇒ x^{2} + 4\sqrt{2}x - 10 = 0$

$⇒ x = \sqrt{2}$\text{or} -$5\sqrt{2}$

So,~$y = 7$~for& $x = - 5\sqrt{2}$

Now we know that~$x = $\text{sec}$\theta = - 5\sqrt{2}$

And~$y = tan\theta = 7$,

So, the value of~${sec}^{2}\theta + tan\theta = 50 + 7 = 57$

$

questions.q: If the vertices and foci of a hyperbola are respectively $\left(\pm 3, 0\right)$~and $\left(\pm 4, 0\right)$& then the parametric equations of that hyperbola are

The vertices and foci of a hyperbola are respectively $\left(\pm 3, 0\right)$ and $\left(\pm 4, 0\right)$

So& $a = 3$ and& $ae = 4$, then $e = \dfrac{4}{3}$

Now we know that

$b^{2} = a^{2} \left(e^{2} - 1\right)$

$⇒ b^{2} = {3}^{2} \left( \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)2 - 1\right)$

$⇒ b^{2} = 16 - 9 = 7$

$⇒ b = \sqrt{7}

So equation of hyperbola is given by \dfrac{x2}{9} - \dfrac{y^{2}}{7} =1$

Now parametric equation of hyperbola is given by $x = a\text{sec \theta}$& y = btan$\theta

So, $ x = 3$\text{sec}\theta$& y = \s$ sqrt{7}tan\theta$

questions.q: Let origin be the centre, $\left(\pm 3, 0\right)$ be the foci and $\dfrac{3}{2}$ be the eccentricity of a hyperbola. Then the line $2x - y - 1 = 0$
options: intersects the hyperbola at two points
passes through the vertex of the hyperbola
questions.solution:
Given,

Origin be the centre, $\left(\pm 3, 0\right)$ be the foci and $\dfrac{3}{2}$ be the eccentricity of a hyperbola,

Now we know that foci is& $\left(\pm ae, 0\right) ≡ \left(\pm3, 0\right)$,

So $ae = 3$ and given& $e = \dfrac{3}{2}$$ then& $a = $\dfrac{1}{2}$$,$$

Now by formula $b^{2} = a^{2} $\left(e^{2} - 1\right)$$ we get& $b = $\dfrac{5}{4}$$

So, equation of hyperbola will be \dfrac{x2}{\dfrac{1}{4}} - \dfrac{y2}{\dfrac{5}{16}} =1$

$⇒ 20x^{2} - y^{2} = 80$

Now putting the value of $y$ from the& line $2x - y - 1 = 0$ in hyperbola to check intersecting or not,

So,& $20x^{2} - \left(2x - 1\right)2 = 80$

$⇒ 16x^{2} + 4x - 81 = 0$

Now discriminant $D = {4}^{2} + 4 \times16 \times81 > 0$, hence line does not intersect the hyperbola.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The locus of a variable point whose chord of contact w.r.t. the hyperbola $\dfrac{x2}{a2} - \dfrac{y2}{b2} =1$ subtends a right angle at the origin is
questions.solution:
Given,

The equation of the given hyperbola is& $\dfrac{x2}{a2} - \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1 ⋯ \left(1\right)$

Now let $\left(h, k\right)$ be the pole of a chord& $PQ$ of the hyperbola

Then the straight line& $PQ$ is the polar of the point& $\left(h, k\right)$ w.r.t. the hyperbola and so its equation is

$\dfrac{xh}{a2} - \dfrac{yk}{b2} =1 ⋯ \left(2\right)$

Now the center of the hyperbola is the origin, let it be point $C$,

Now making& $\left(1\right)$ homogeneous with the help of& $\left(2\right)$, the combined equation of& $CP$ and& $CQ$ is

$\dfrac{x2}{a2} - \dfrac{y2}{b2} =\left(\dfrac{xh}{a2} - \dfrac{yk}{b2}\right)2 ⋯ \left(3\right)$

Now the chord $PQ$ subtends a right angle at& $\left(0, 0\right)$

Therefore the lines $CP$ and& $CQ$ given by& $\left(3\right)$ are perpendicular and so in the equation& $\left(3\right)$, we have the coefficient of $x^{2} +$coefficient of $y^{2} = 0$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{1}{a2} - \dfrac{h2}{a4}\right) + \left(\dfrac{- 1}{b2} - \dfrac{k2}{b4}\right) =0$

$⇒ \dfrac{h2}{a4} + \dfrac{k2}{b4} = \dfrac{1}{a2} - \dfrac{1}{b2}$

Thus locus is

$\dfrac{x2}{a4} + \dfrac{y2}{b4} = \dfrac{1}{a2} - \dfrac{1}{b2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the latus rectum subtends a right angle at center of the hyperbola, then its eccentricity is
questions.solution: Given, latus rectum of hyperbola subtends 90º at its centre. Let there be a hyperbola $\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ So, eccentricity, $e=\sqrt{1+\frac{b^2}{a^2}}$ End points of latusrectum are L= $\left(a e, \frac{b^2}{a}\right) \text{ and } L^{\prime}=\left(a e, \frac{-b^2}{a}\right)$$ \\ Centre = (0, 0) \because \quad \angle L C L^{\prime}=90^{{}^{\circ}} Then, in \Delta$ L C L^{\prime}$, by using Pythagoras theorem, \begin{aligned} (L C)^2+\left(L^{\prime} C\right)^2 & =\left(L L^{\prime}\right)^2 \\ (a e-0)^2 & +\left(\frac{b^2}{a}-0\right)^2+(a e-0)^2+\left(\frac{-b^2}{a}-0\right)^2 \\ & =\left(\frac{2 b^2}{a}\right)^2 \end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & 2\left(a^2 e^2+\frac{b^4}{a^2}\right)=\frac{4 b^4}{a^2} \Rightarrow \frac{2 b^4}{a^2}=2 a^2 e^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad b^4=a^4 e^2 \\ & {\left[a^2\left(e^2-1\right)\right]^2=a^4 e^2 \quad\left\{\because b^2=a^2\left(e^2-1\right)\right\}} \\ & a^4\left(e^2-1\right)^2=a^4 e^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad\left(e^2-1\right)^2=e^2 \Rightarrow e^2-1= \pm e \\ & \Rightarrow e^2 \pm e-1=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad e=\frac{ \pm 1 \pm \sqrt{1+4}}{2}=\frac{ \pm 1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2} \\ & \end{aligned} $\because e$ can't be negative, hence $$e=\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{2}.$

questions.q: In a hyperbola, if the length of transverse axis is twice that of the conjugate axis, then the distance between its directrices is..... units.
questions.solution:
Given, in a hyperbola, the length of transverse axis is twice that of the conjugate axis. The equation of standard hyperbola is
$\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1\because$ Length of transverse axis $=2 \times$ length of conjugate axis
$2 a=2 \times 2 b\begin{array}{lll}\Rightarrow & a & =2 b \\ \because & b^2 & =a^2\left(e^2-1\right)\end{array}
$$\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow$& $\frac{a^2}{4}=$a^2$\left($e^2-1\right) \\ \Rightarrow & e²=1+$\frac{1}{4}=\frac{5}{4}\end{array}\Rightarrow \quad e=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\therefore$ Distance between its directrix $=\frac{2 a}{e}=\frac{2(2 b)}{\sqrt{5} / 2}=\frac{8 b}{\sqrt{5}}$

questions.solution:

Then, equation of line is $\begin{aligned}$& y-y_1=m$\left($x-x_1\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \quad y+2=m(x-1) \\ & y+2=m x-m \\ & \Rightarrow \quad $\frac{m x-y}{2+m}=$1 \\ & \end{aligned} Use Eq. (ii) in Eq. (i) as follows, $\begin{aligned}$& 3 x²-y²-2 x$\left(\frac{m x-y}{2+m}\right)+$4 y$\left(\frac{m x-y}{2+m}\right)=$0 \\ & \Rightarrow 3(2+m) x²-(2+m) y²-2 x(m x-y) \\ &+ 4 y(m x-y)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x²(6+3 m-2 m)-y²(2+m+4)+x y \\ &(4 m+2)=0 \end{aligned} General equation of curve is a x²+2 h x y+b y²+2 g x+2 f y+c=0 Compare Eqs. (iii) and (iv), a=6+m, b=-6-m This gives, $a+b=0\Rightarrow$ Angle subtended by these two lines at origin is $90^{{}^{\circ}}$.

questions.solution:
Given hyperbola $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$

Asymptotes of hyperbola are $\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} = 0 . . . \left(I\right), \dfrac{x}{a} - \dfrac{y}{b} = 0 . . . \left(II\right)$

Tangent at $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$ is $\dfrac{x{x}_{1}}{{a}^{2}} - \dfrac{y{y}_{1}}{{b}^{2}} = 1 . . . . \left(III\right)$

We know that area formed by a triangle with asymptotes and any tangent is equal to $ab$.

$⇒ ab = {a}^{2}tan\alpha$

$⇒ b = atan\alpha$

Eccentricity of hyperbola are $e = \sqrt{\dfrac{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}}$

$⇒ e = \sqrt{\dfrac{{a}^{2} + {a}^{2}{tan}^{2}\alpha}{{a}^{2}}} = \sqrt{1 + {tan}^{2}\alpha} = sec\alpha .$

If the normals drawn to the hyperbola \(x y=4\) at \($\left(\alpha_$i, \beta_i\right)(i=1,2,3,4)\) are concurrent at$ the point \((a, b)\), then
\(\frac{\left(\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3+\alpha_4\right)}{\left(\beta_1+\beta_2+\beta_3+\beta_4\right)}\left(\alpha_$1 \alpha_2 \alpha_3 \alpha_4\right)=\)

\sum\left(\frac{\alpha_1 \alpha_2}{4}\right)=0 \\
\sum \frac{\alpha_1 \alpha_2 \alpha_3}{8}=\frac{-b}{2} \text{$ and $} \frac{\alpha_1 \alpha_2 \alpha_3 \alpha_4}{16}=-1 \\
\because \beta_1+\beta_2+\beta_3+\beta_4=\frac{4}{\alpha_1}+\frac{4}{\alpha_2}+\frac{4}{\alpha_3}+\frac{4}{\alpha_4}
\end{gathered} =4 \frac{\Sigma \alpha_1 \alpha_2 \alpha_3}{\alpha_1 \alpha_2 \alpha_3 \alpha_4}\)
\(=4 \frac{-b / 2 \times 8}{-16}=b\)
\begin{aligned}\frac{\left.\therefore \alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3+\alpha_4\right)}{\beta_1+\beta_2+\beta_3+\beta_4}& \left(\alpha_1 \alpha_2 \alpha_3 \alpha_4\right) \\
= & \frac{a(-16)}{b}=-16 \frac{a}{b}
\end{aligned}$
Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.q: A hyperbola with centre at $(0,0)$ has its transverse axis along $X$-axis whose length is $12$. If $(8,2)$ is a point on the hyperbola, then its eccentricity is<gwmw style="display:none;"></gwmw>
questions.solution:
Consider the equation of the hyperbola be $\dfrac{x2}{a2} - \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1$
It is given that the centre of the hyperbola is $\left(0, 0\right)$ and its transverse axis is along $x$-axis and its length is $12$.
$2a = 12$
$a = 6$

Substitute this value in the equation of a hyperbola.
$\dfrac{x2}{62} - \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1$
The above equation passes through the point~$\left(8, 2\right)$
$\dfrac{82}{62} - \dfrac{22}{b2} = 1$
$\dfrac{64}{36} - \dfrac{4}{b2} = 1$
After simplification,
$b = \dfrac{6}{7}$
The equation of hyperbola becomes,

$\dfrac{x2}{62} - \dfrac{y2}{\left(\dfrac{6}{7}\right)2} = 1$
$\dfrac{x2}{36} - \dfrac{7y^{2}}{36} = 1$
The eccentricity of a hyperbola is,

$e = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{a2}{b2}}$

$e = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{62}{\left(\dfrac{6}{7}\right)2}}$

$e = \sqrt{\dfrac{8}{7}}$

$e = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{7}$

questions.q: The locus of the mid-points of the chords of the circle $x^2+y^2=16$ which are the tangents to the hyperbola $9 x^2-16 y^2=144$ is
questions.solution:
Equation of chord with mid-point $(h, k)$ to the circle $x^2+y^2=16$ is $T=S_1 \begin{gathered}$h x+k y-16=h²+k²-16 \\
y=-$\frac{h}{k}$ x+$\left(\frac{h^2+k^2}{k}\right)
\end{gathered}For hyperbola 9 x^2-16 y^2=144$
\Rightarrow \quad $\frac{x^2}{16}-\frac{y^2}{9}=1

As we know that, condition$ of tangency of a line y=m x+c$ is $a^2 m^2-b^2=c^2$

So,

\begin{aligned}\text{ So, }& & 16\left(-\frac{h}{k}\right)^2-9 & =\left(\frac{h^2+k^2}{k}\right)^2 \\
\Rightarrow & & 16 h²-9 k² & =\left(h^2+k²\right)^2
\end{aligned}

Replace $ h, k$ by $x, y$
\therefore \quad 16 x²-9 y²=\left(x^2+y²\right)^2
$

questions.q: The equation of a tangent to the hyperbola \(16 x²-25 y²-96 x+100 y-356=0\) which makes an angle \(45^{{}^{\circ}}\) with its transverse axis is
questions.solution:
Given equation of hyperbola
\begin{aligned}& 16 x²-25 y²-96 x+100 y-356=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad $\frac{(x-3)^2}{25}-\frac{(y-2)^2}{16}=$1 \quad \ldots (i)
\end{aligned}\)
Now equation$ of $tangent to the hyperbola (i) having slope ' 1 ' is
\begin{aligned} y-2 &$=1(x-3)+\sqrt{25(1)-16}$\\
\Rightarrow \quad y-2 & =x-3+3 \\
y-2 & =x-3+3 $\text{$ or }y-2=x-3-3 \\
$\text{ or } \quad$x-y-4 & =0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad x-y+2 & =0
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (1) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $If the eccentricity of a hyperbola is \dfrac{5}{3},$ then the eccentricity of its conjugate hyperbola is
questions.solution:
Let the eccentricity of hyperbola and conjugate hyperbola be ${e}_{1} \text{ and } {e}_{2}$ respectively. Then,

$1{e}_{1}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{{e}_{2}^{2}} = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{5}{3}\right)^{2}} + 1{e}_{2}^{2} = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{9}{25} + 1{e}_{2}^{2} = 1$

$⇒ 1{e}_{2}^{2} = 1 - \dfrac{9}{25}$

$⇒ 1{e}_{2}^{2} = \dfrac{16}{25}$

$⇒ {e}_{2} = \pm \dfrac{5}{4}$

But, eccentricity of hyperbola is never less than one. Hence, ${e}_{2} = \dfrac{5}{4}$.

questions.q: If the eccentricity of a hyperbola is $\frac{5}{3}, then the eccentricity of its conjugate hyperbola is$
questions.solution:
Eccentricity of given hyperbola $=\frac{5}{3}$
Let, eccentricity of its conjugate hyperbola $=e$
So, $\frac{1}{\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^2}+\frac{1}{e^2}=1\Rightarrow \quad \frac{9}{25}+\frac{1}{e^2}=1 \quad \Rightarrow \frac{1}{e^2}=1-\frac{9}{25}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{e^2}=\frac{16}{25} \Rightarrow e^2=\frac{25}{16}$
\Rightarrow \quad e=$\frac{5}{4}$ Hence, eccentricity of conjugate hyperbola $=\frac{5}{4}$

& & (3+4-2)(2+1+1) & =\lambda \\

& (3 x+4 y-2)(2 x+y+1)=20 \\

y=$\frac{-l}{m}+\frac{1}{m}$ Which is of the form $y=m x+c$
Since, the lines $y=m x+c$ will be normal to the hyperbola $\begin{aligned}& \frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1, \text{ if } c^2=\frac{m^2\left(a^2+b^2\right)^2}{a^2-b^2 m^2}\\
& \therefore \quad\left(\frac{1}{m}\right)^2=\frac{\left(-\frac{l}{m}\right)^2\left(a^2+b^2\right)^2}{a^2-b^2\left(-\frac{l}{m}\right)^2}
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{m^2}=\frac{\frac{l^2}{m^2}\left(a^2+b^2\right)^2}{\frac{m^2 a^2-l^2 b^2}{m^2}} \\ & \frac{1}{m^2}=\frac{l^2\left(a^2+b^2\right)^2}{m^2 a^2-l^2 b^2} \\ & a^2 m^2-b^2 l^2=l^2 m^2\left(a^2+b^2\right)^2\end{aligned}$

We have, line, $y=m x+2$... (i)
Hyperbola,
$4 x^2-9 y^2=36... (ii)$
On solving eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$x^2\left(4-9 m^2\right)-36 m x-72=0$
Since, this line is a tangent of hyperbola
$\begin{array}{ll}
\therefore & \mathrm{D}=\mathrm{b}^2-4 \mathrm{ac}=0 \\

questions.q: The foci of the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ and the hyperbola $\frac{x^2}{144}-\frac{y^2}{81}=\frac{1}{25}$ coincide. Then, the value of $b^2$ is
questions.solution:
Equation of ellipse, $\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ 
Eccentricity,
$\therefore \quad e=\sqrt{1-\frac{b^2}{16}}=\frac{\sqrt{16-b^2}}{4}$
So, the focus will be $\left( \pm \sqrt{16-b^2}, 0\right)$ Also, the equation of hyperbola,
$\frac{x^2}{144}-\frac{y^2}{81}=\frac{1}{25} \Rightarrow \frac{x^2}{\left(\frac{144}{25}\right)}-\frac{y^2}{\left(\frac{81}{25}\right)}=1\therefore \quad e=\sqrt{1+\frac{b^2}{a^2}}=\sqrt{1+\frac{\frac{81}{25}}{\frac{144}{25}}}= \pm \frac{15}{12}$
So, the focus will be
$\left( \pm \frac{12}{5} \times \frac{15}{12}, 0\right) \text{ i.e., }( \pm 3,0)$
On comparing the focus of ellipse with hyperbola, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \sqrt{16-b^2}=3 \\
& 16-b^2=9 \\
& b^2=7
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $A hyperbola passing through a focus of the ellipse \frac{x^2}{169}+\frac{y^2}{25}=1$. Its transverse and conjugate axes coincide respectively with the major and minor axes of the ellipse. The product of eccentricities is 1. Then, the equation of the hyperbola is
questions.solution:
Let the equation of hyperbola be

$\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=$1

Given equation of ellipse is

$\frac{x^2}{(13)^2}+\frac{y^2}{(5)^2}=$1

Here,

$\begin{aligned}$& $\text{ Here, } \quad$a=13, b=5 \\
& \therefore \quad e=$\sqrt{1-\frac{b^2}{a^2}}$\\
& \therefore \quad=$\sqrt{1-\frac{25}{169}}=\sqrt{\frac{144}{169}}=\frac{12}{13}$\\
& \therefore $\text{ Focus }( \pm$a e, 0)=$\left( \pm$13 $\times \frac{12}{13},$0\right) \\
& \quad=( $\pm$12,0)
\end{aligned}

Since, Eq. (i) passes through $( \pm 12,0)$.

$\begin{array}{rrrl}
\therefore& \frac{144}{a^2}-\frac{0}{b^2}=1 \\
\Rightarrow & a²=144 \\
\Rightarrow & a= \pm12
\end{array}$

Now eccentricity of $hyperbola\begin{aligned}$e^{\prime} & =$\sqrt{1+\frac{b^2}{a^2}}$\\
& =$\sqrt{1+\frac{b^2}{144}}
\end{aligned}$According to the equation,

$\begin{array}{rlrl}& e^{\prime}=1 \\
\Rightarrow & & \frac{12}{13} \times$ \sqrt{1+$\frac{b^2}{144}}& =1 \\
\Rightarrow & & \sqrt{1+\frac{b^2}{144}$}& =$\frac{13}{12}\\
\Rightarrow & & 1+\frac{b^2}{144}$& =$\frac{169}{144}\\
\Rightarrow & & \frac{b^2}{144}$& =$\frac{169}{144}-1 \\
\Rightarrow & & \frac{b^2}{144}$& =$\frac{25}{144}\\
b² & =25
\end{array}$\thereforeEquation$ of hyperbola is

\frac{x^2}{144}-\frac{y^2}{25}$=$1
$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the focii of the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{25}+\frac{y^2}{16}=1$ and the hyperbola $\frac{x^2}{4}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ coincide, then $b^2$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, equation of ellipse is

$\frac{x^2}{25}+\frac{y^2}{16}=1

and equation of hyperbola is

\frac{x^2}{4}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1

eccentricity of ellipse

\begin{aligned}$& b²=a²$\left(1-e²\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 16=25\left(1-e²\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad e²=1-\frac{16}{25}=\frac{9}{25}$\\
& \Rightarrow \quad e= $\pm \frac{3}{5}$\\
&
\end{aligned}

Focii of the ellipse $=( \pm a e, 0)=( \pm 3,0)$ which coincide with focii of the hyperbola.
Let $e_1$ be the eccentricity of the hyperbola.

$\begin{array}{ll}
\therefore$& $\pm$ a e_1= $\pm3 \\
\Rightarrow & e_1=\frac{3}{2}
\end{array}$ Now, $\quad b^2=a^2   \left(e_1^2-1\right)
\begin{array}{cc}
\Rightarrow & $ b^2=4\$ left(\frac{9}{4}-1\right)=4 \times \frac{5}{4}$$\\
\Rightarrow & b²=5
\end{array}

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $x=9$ is a chord of contact of the hyperbola $x^2-y^2=9$, then the equation of the tangent at one of the points of contact is
questions.solution:
Given that, $x=9$ is a chord of contact of hyperbola. $\begin{aligned}& x²-y²=9 \\
& \text{ put } x=9, \quad 81-y²=9 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad y²=72 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad y=6 \sqrt{2} \text{ or }-6 \sqrt{2}\\
&
\end{aligned} $\therefore$ Points are $(9,6 $\sqrt{2})$ and (9,-6 $\sqrt{2})
Now, differentiating Eq. (i) w.r.t. $ x$, we get \begin{aligned}& 2 x-2 y \frac{d y}{d x}=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{x}{y}\\
& \text{ at }(9,6 \sqrt{2}) \quad\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)_{(9,6 \sqrt{2})}=\frac{9}{6 \sqrt{2}}=\frac{3}{2 \sqrt{2}}\\
& \text{$ and $at }(9-6 \sqrt{2})\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)_{(9,-6 \sqrt{2})}=-\frac{3}{2 \sqrt{2}}\\
&
\end{aligned}$\therefore$ Equation of tangent at $(9,6 $\sqrt{2}) is \begin{aligned}
( y-6 \sqrt{2})& =\frac{3}{2 \sqrt{2}}( x-9) \\
\Rightarrow \quad 2 \sqrt{2} y-24 & =3 x-27 \\
\Rightarrow \quad 3 x-2 \sqrt{2} y-3 & =0
\end{aligned}$ and equation of tangent at(9,-6 $\sqrt{2}) is \begin{aligned}
( y+6 \sqrt{2})& =\frac{-3}{2 \sqrt{2}}( x-9) \\
\Rightarrow \quad 2 \sqrt{2} y+24 & =-3 x+27 \\
\Rightarrow \quad 3 x+2 \sqrt{2} y-3 & =0
\end{aligned}
$

questions.q: Equation of one of the tangents passing through $(2,8)$ to the hyperbola $5 x^2-y^2=5$ is
questions.solution:
Given hyperbola is $5 x^2-y^2=5$ or It can be rewritten as
$\frac{x^2}{1}-\frac{y^2}{5}=1$
Here,
$\therefore$ Equation of tangent is
$\begin{aligned} & y=m x \pm \sqrt{a^2 m^2-b^2} \\ & y=m x \pm \sqrt{1 m^2-5}\end{aligned}$
But point $(2,8)$ lies on it.
$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad 8=2 m \pm \sqrt{m^2-5} \\ & \Rightarrow(8-2 m)= \pm \sqrt{m^2-5}\end{aligned}$
On squaring both sides, we get
$$\begin{array}{rlrl} & 64+4 m^2-32 m & =m^2-5 \\ \Rightarrow \quad 3 m^2-32 m+69 & =0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad & (3 m-23)(m-3) & =0 \\ \Rightarrow & m & =3, $\frac{23}{3}$\end{array}$
On putting $m=3$ in Eq. (i), we get
\begin{aligned}$y & =3 x $\pm \sqrt{3^2-5}=$3 x $\pm$2 \\ \Rightarrow & y=3 x+2 $\text{ and }$y=3 x-2\end{aligned}

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area (in sq units) of the equilateral triangle formed by the tangent at $(\sqrt{3}, 0)$ to the hyperbola $x^2-3 y^2=3$ with the pair of asymptotes of the hyperbola is
questions.solution:
Given equation of hyperbola is $x^2-3 y^2=3\therefore$ Equation of tangent at point $(\sqrt{3}, 0)$ is
$\begin{aligned} & S_1=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad & x \sqrt{3}-3 y \times 0=3\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & & x \sqrt{3} & =3 \\ \Rightarrow & & x & =\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$
The asympotes of given hyperbolas are
$x+\sqrt{3} y=0 and x-\sqrt{3} y=0$
On solving Eqs. (i), (ii) and (iii), we get
$(0,0),(\sqrt{3},-1) and (\sqrt{3}, 1)\therefore$ Area of triangle formed by joining the above points
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{array}{rrr}0 & 0 & 1 \\ \sqrt{3} & -1 & 0 \\ \sqrt{3} & 1 & 0\end{array}\right| \\ & =\frac{1}{2}[1(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{3})]=\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \sqrt{3}=\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The angle between the asymptotes of the hyperbola $x^2-3 y^2=3$ is
questions.solution:
Given equation of hyperbola is $\begin{aligned} x^2-3 y^2 & =3 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{x^2}{3}-\frac{y^2}{1} & =1 \end{aligned}$ Here, $a^2=3$ and $b^2=1, a > b$. Now, the equation of asymptote of this hyperbola is, $\begin{aligned} y & = \pm \frac{b}{a} x \\ \Rightarrow \quad y & = \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} x\end{aligned}$
Let slope of asymptote (i) is, $m_1=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ and slope of asymptote (ii) is, $m_2=\frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}}$ Let $\theta$ be the angle between both asymptote, then $\tan \theta=\left|\frac{m_1-m_2}{1+m_1 m_2}\right|=\left|\frac{1 / \sqrt{3}+1 / \sqrt{3}}{1-1 / 3}\right|\begin{array}{cc}\Rightarrow & \tan \theta=\left|\frac{2 / \sqrt{3}}{2 / 3}\right|=\sqrt{3} \\ \Rightarrow & \tan \theta=\tan 60^{{}^{\circ}} \\ \Rightarrow & \theta=\pi / 3\end{array}$

questions.q: The product of the perpendicular distances from any point on the hyperbola $\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ to its asymptotes is
questions.solution:
Let $(a \sec \theta, b \tan \theta)$ be any point on the hyperbola $\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$
The equation of the asymptotes of the given hyperbola are
$\left(\frac{x}{a}+\frac{y}{b}\right)=0 \text{ and }\left(\frac{x}{a}-\frac{y}{b}\right)=0$
Now, $P_1=$ length of the perpendicular from $(a \sec \theta, b \tan \theta$ ) on

questions.solution:
If $l x+m y+n=0$ is normal to the hyperbola
$\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$
Then $\frac{a^2}{l^2}-\frac{b^2}{m^2}=\frac{\left(a^2+b^2\right)^2}{n^2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $If the eccentricity of a hyperbola is \sqrt{3}$; then the eccentricity of its conjugate hyperbola is :
questions.solution:
Let $e$ and $e^{\prime}$ are the eccentricities of a hyperbola and its conjugate hyperbola.
We know that
$\frac{1}{e^2}+\frac{1}{\left(e^{\prime}\right)^2}=1\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{\left(e^{\prime}\right)^2}=1\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{\left(e^{\prime}\right)^2}=\frac{2}{3} \Rightarrow e^{\prime}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The product of the lengths of perpendiculars drawn from any point on the hyperbola $x^2-2 y^2-2=0$ to its asymptotes is :
questions.solution:
Equation of hyperbola is
$x^2-2 y^2=2\Rightarrow \quad \frac{x^2}{2}-\frac{y^2}{1}=1$
Here, $a^2=2, b^2=1$
Equation of asymptotes to the hyperbola
$\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1 \text{ is } \frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=0\therefore \quad \frac{x}{a}-\frac{y}{b}=0$ and $\frac{x}{a}+\frac{y}{b}=0$
Let $P(a \sec \theta, b \tan \theta)$ be any point, then the product of length of perpendiculars
$=\frac{\left[\frac{a \sec \theta}{a}+\frac{b \tan \theta}{b}\right]}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{a^2}+\frac{1}{b^2}}} \frac{\left[\frac{a \sec \theta}{a}+\frac{b \tan \theta}{b}\right]}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{a^2}+\frac{1}{b^2}}}=\frac{\sec ^2 \theta-\tan ^2 \theta}{\frac{1}{a^2}+\frac{1}{b^2}}=\frac{1}{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{1}}=\frac{2}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The products of lengths of perpendiculars from any point of hyperbola $x^2-y^2=8$ to its asymptotes, is
questions.solution:
We have the asymptotes are
$x^2-y^2=0 \Rightarrow x= \pm y$
i.e. $x+y=0$ and $x-y=0$
The product of length of perpendiculars
$=\left(\frac{x-y}{\sqrt{1^2+1^2}}\right)\left(\frac{x+y}{\sqrt{1^2+1^2}}\right)=\frac{x^2-y^2}{\sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{2}}=\frac{8}{2}=4$

represents

questions.q:
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{4 x^2+5}{(x-2)^4}=\frac{A}{(x-2)}+\frac{B}{(X-2)^2}+\frac{C}{(X-2)^3}+\frac{D}{(X-2)^4} \text{ then } \\
& \sqrt{\frac{A}{C}+\frac{B}{C}+\frac{D}{C}}=
\end{aligned}$
questions.solution:
$\frac{4 x^2+5}{(x-2)^4}=\frac{A}{x-2}+\frac{B}{(x-2)^2}+\frac{C}{(x-2)^3}+\frac{D}{(x-2)^4}\Rightarrow A(x-2)^3+B(x-2)^2+C(x-2)+D=4 x^2+5$
If $x=2 \Rightarrow D=21$
Co-efficient of $x^3, A=0$
Constant term, $4 B-2 C+21=5 \Rightarrow 4 B-2 C=-16$
Co-efficient of $x^2, B=4$
So, $16-2 C=-16 \Rightarrow C=16$
Now, $\sqrt{\frac{A}{C}+\frac{B}{C}+\frac{D}{C}}=\sqrt{\frac{A+B+D}{C}}=\sqrt{\frac{4+21}{16}}=\frac{5}{4}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int \frac{\sqrt[4]{x}}{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt[4]{x}} d x=\frac{2}{3}\left[A \sqrt[4]{x^3}+B \sqrt[4]{x^2}+C \sqrt[4]{x}+D \log (1+\sqrt[4]{x})\right]+K$ then $\frac{2}{3}(A+B+C+D)=$
questions.solution:
Let $I=\int \frac{\sqrt[4]{x}}{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt[4]{x}} d x$ Let $u=\sqrt[4]{x} \Rightarrow d u=\frac{1}{4 x^{3 / 4}} d x$ and $\sqrt{x}=u^2 \Rightarrow x=u^4\begin{aligned} & \therefore I=4 \int \frac{u^3}{u+1} d u=4 \int\left(u^2-u+1-\frac{1}{u+1}\right) d u \\ & \Rightarrow I=\frac{4}{3} u^3-\frac{4 u^2}{2}+4 u-4 \log (u+1)+K \\ & \Rightarrow I=\frac{4}{3} \sqrt[4]{x^3}-2 \sqrt[4]{x^2}+4 \sqrt[4]{x}-4 \log (1+\sqrt[4]{x})+K \\ & \Rightarrow I=\frac{2}{3}\left[2 \sqrt[4]{x^3}-3 \sqrt[4]{x^2}+6 \sqrt[4]{x}-6 \log (1+\sqrt[4]{x})\right]+K \end{aligned}$
Comparing with $\begin{aligned} & -\left[A \sqrt[4]{x^3}+B \sqrt[4]{x^2}+C \sqrt[4]{x}+D \log (1+\sqrt[4]{x})\right]+K \\ & A=2, B=-3, C=6, D=-6 \\ & \therefore \frac{2}{3}(A+B+C+D)=-\frac{2}{3} \end{aligned}$

questions.solution: $I=\int \sin ^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\frac{x-a}{x}}\right) d x\begin{aligned} & \text{ Let } x=a \sec ^2 \theta \Rightarrow d x=2 a \sec ^2 \theta \tan \theta \mathrm{ d} \theta \\ & I=\int \sin ^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\frac{a \sec ^2 \theta-a}{a \sec ^2 \theta}}\right) \cdot 2 a \sec ^2 \theta \tan \theta d \theta \\ & \Rightarrow I=\int \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{\tan \theta}{\sec \theta}\right) \cdot 2 a \sec ^2 \theta \tan \theta d \theta \\ & \Rightarrow I=\int \theta \cdot 2 a \sec ^2 \theta \tan \theta d \theta=\theta a \sec ^2 \theta-a \int \sec ^2 \theta d \theta \\ & \Rightarrow I=\theta a \sec ^2 \theta-a \tan \theta+C=x \cos ^{-1} \sqrt{\frac{a}{x}}-\sqrt{a x-a^2}+C\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\int \frac{\sin x \cos x}{\sqrt{\cos ^4 x-\sin ^4 x}} d x=-\frac{f(x)}{2}+c$, then domain of $f(x)$ is
questions.solution:
$I=\int \frac{\sin x \cos x}{\sqrt{\cos ^4 x-\sin ^4 x}} d x \Rightarrow I=\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{\sin 2 x}{\sqrt{\cos 2 x}} d x$ Let $\cos 2 x=t \Rightarrow-2 \sin 2 x d x=d t\therefore I=\frac{-1}{4} \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{t}} d t \Rightarrow I=\frac{-1}{2} \sqrt{t}+C \Rightarrow I=\frac{-\sqrt{\cos 2 x}}{2}+C$
On comparing with $\frac{-f(x)}{2}+C \Rightarrow f(x)=\sqrt{\cos 2 x}$ For domain : $\cos 2 x \geq 0\Rightarrow\left(2 n-\frac{1}{2}\right) \pi \leq 2 x \leq\left(2 n+\frac{1}{2}\right) \pi\Rightarrow(4 n-1) \frac{\pi}{4} \leq x \leq(4 n+1) \frac{\pi}{2}, n=0,1,2, \ldots .$.

questions.q: If $A=\int_0^{\infty} \frac{1+x^2}{1+x^4} d x, \quad B=\int_0^1 \frac{1+x^2}{1+x^4} d x$, then
questions.solution:
$A=\int_0^{\infty} \frac{1+x^2}{1+x^4} d x, B=\int_0^1 \frac{1+x^2}{1+x^4} d x$
Let $I=\int \frac{1+x^2}{1+x^4} d x=\int \frac{1+x^2}{\left(x^2-\sqrt{2} x+1\right)\left(x^2+\sqrt{2} x+1\right)} d x$
By partial fraction
$\begin{aligned}
& I=\int\left(\frac{1}{2\left(x^2+\sqrt{2} x+1\right)}+\frac{1}{2\left(x^2-\sqrt{2} x+1\right)}\right) d x \\
& \Rightarrow I=\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{1}{x^2+\sqrt{2} x+1} d x+\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{1}{x^2-\sqrt{2} x+1} d x \\
& \Rightarrow I=\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{d x}{\left(x+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2+\frac{1}{2}}+\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{d x}{\left(x-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2+\frac{1}{2}} \\
& \Rightarrow I=\frac{1}{2} \times \sqrt{2} \tan ^{-1} \frac{\left(x+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}} \\
& +\frac{1}{2} \times \sqrt{2} \frac{\tan ^{-1}\left(x-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}+C
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow I=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \tan ^{-1}(\sqrt{2} x+1)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \tan ^{-1}(\sqrt{2} x-1)+C \\ & \Rightarrow I=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \tan ^{-1} \frac{\sqrt{2} x}{1-x^2}+C \\ & A=[I]_0^{\infty}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left[\tan ^{-1} \frac{\sqrt{2} x}{1-x^2}\right]_0^{\infty}=\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{2}} \\ & B=[I]_0^1=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left[\tan ^{-1} \frac{\sqrt{2} x}{1-x^2}\right]_0^1=\frac{\pi}{2 \sqrt{2}} \\ & \therefore 2 B=A\end{aligned}$

Let $x^2+2 x=t \Rightarrow(x+1) d x=\frac{d t}{2}I=\frac{1}{2} \int e^{4 t-4} \cos (3 t-4) d t$

questions.q: If $\int \log \left(6 \sin ^2 x+17 \sin x+12\right)^{\cos x} d x=f(x)+c$ then, $f\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=$
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{I}=\int \log \left(6 \sin ^2 x+17 \sin x+12\right)^{\cos x} d x$
Let $\sin x=t \Rightarrow \cos x d x=d t\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}=\int \log \left(6 t^2+17 t+12\right) d t \\ & \mathrm{I}=t \log \left(6 t^2+17 t+12\right)-\int \frac{t(12 t+17)}{6 t^2+17 t+12} d t \\ & \mathrm{I}=t \log \left(6 t^2+17 t+12\right)-\int 2 d t+\int \frac{17 t+24}{6 t^2+17 t+12} d t \\ & \mathrm{I}=t \log \left(6 t^2+17 t+12\right)-2 t+\frac{17}{12} \int \frac{12 t+17}{6 t^2+17 t+12} d t \\ & \quad-\frac{1}{12} \int \frac{1}{6 t^2+17 t+12} d t \\ & \mathrm{I}=t \log \left(6 t^2+17 t+12\right)-2 t+\frac{17}{12} \log \left(6 t^2+17 t+12\right) \\ & -\frac{1}{4} \int \frac{d t}{3 t+4}+\frac{1}{6} \int \frac{d t}{2 t+3} \end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}=t \log \left(6 t^2+17 t+12\right)-2 t+\frac{17}{12} \log \left(6 t^2+17 t+12\right) \\ & -\frac{\log (3 t+4)}{12}+\frac{\log (2 t+3)}{12}+\mathrm{C} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{I}=\frac{\left[$\begin{array}{c} (12 $\sin x+17$) $\log$((2 $\sin x+3$)(3 $\sin x+4$)] \\ -$\log$(3 $\sin x+4$)+$\log$(2 $\sin x+3$)-24 $\sin x$ \end{array}$\right]}{12}+\mathrm{c}-\frac{17}{6}\left\{\because C=c-\frac{17}{6}\right\} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{29 \log [35]-\log 7+\log 5-24+28 \log 7-28 \log 7}{12}-\frac{17}{6} \\ & =\frac{29 \log \frac{35}{7}+28 \log 7+\log 5-24}{12}-\frac{17}{6}=\frac{30 \log 5+28 \log 7-24}{12}-\frac{17}{6} \\ & =\frac{1}{6}[15 \log 5+14 \log 7-29] \end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
$I=\int \frac{1}{\left(1+x^2\right) \sqrt{x^2+2}} d x$
Let $x=\sqrt{2} \tan u \Rightarrow d x=\sqrt{2} \sec ^2 u d v\begin{aligned} & \therefore \mathrm{I}=\sqrt{2} \int \frac{\sec ^2 u}{\left(2 \tan ^2 u+1\right) \sqrt{2 \tan ^2 u+2}} d u \\ & \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{\sec u}{2 \tan ^2 u+1} d u \end{aligned}$
$\mathrm{I}=\int-\cot u \operatorname{cosec} u\left(-\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosec}^2 u+1}\right) d u$
Let $\mathrm{v}=\operatorname{cosec} \mathrm{u} \Rightarrow d v=-\cot u \operatorname{cosec} u d u\begin{aligned} & \therefore \mathrm{I}=-\int \frac{1}{v^2+1} d v=-\tan ^{-1} v+c \\ & \mathrm{I}=-\tan ^{-1}(\operatorname{cosec} u)+\mathrm{c}=-\tan ^{-1} \frac{\sqrt{x^2+2}}{|x|}+c \end{aligned}$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}=\int \sin ^4 x \cos ^4 x d x=\frac{1}{16} \int(\sin 2 x)^4 d x \\ & \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{16} \int \frac{[1-\cos 4 x]^2}{4} d x=\frac{1}{64} \int\left[1+\cos ^2 4 x-2 \cos 4 x\right] d x \\ & \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{64} \int\left[1+\left(\frac{1+\cos 8 x}{2}\right)-2 \cos 4 x\right] d x \\ & \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{128} \int(2+1+\cos 8 x-4 \cos 4 x) d x \\ & \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{128}\left[3 x+\frac{\sin 8 x}{8}-\frac{4 \sin 4 x}{4}\right]+c \\ & \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{128}\left[3 x+\frac{2 \sin 4 x \cos 4 x}{8}-\sin 4 x\right]+c \\ & \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{128}\left[3 x+\frac{2 \sin 2 x \cos 2 x}{4}\left\{\left(1-2 \sin ^2 2 x\right)-4\right\}\right]+c \\ & \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{256}\left[6 x-2 \sin ^3 2 x \cos 2 x-3 \sin 2 x \cos 2 x\right]+\mathrm{c}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\int \frac{1}{1-\cos x} d x=\tan \left(\frac{x}{\alpha}+\beta\right)+c$, then one of the values of $\frac{\pi \alpha}{4}-\beta$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int \frac{1}{1-\cos x} d x=\tan \left(\frac{x}{\alpha}+\beta\right)+c \\ & \Rightarrow \int \frac{1}{2 \sin ^2 \frac{x}{2}} d x=\tan \left(\frac{x}{\alpha}+\beta\right)+c \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} \int \operatorname{cosec}^2 \frac{x}{2} d x=\tan \left(\frac{x}{\alpha}+\beta\right)+c \\ & -\cot \frac{x}{2}+c=\tan \left(\frac{x}{\alpha}+\beta\right)+c \\ & \tan \left(\frac{x}{2}-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\tan \left(\frac{x}{\alpha}+\beta\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \alpha=2, \beta=\frac{-\pi}{2} \therefore \frac{\pi \alpha}{4}-\beta=\frac{\pi}{2}+\frac{\pi}{2}=\pi\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $\int \frac{d x}{x\left(x^4+1\right)}=$
questions.solution: $\mathrm{I}=\int \frac{d x \times x^3}{x\left(x^4+1\right) \times x^3} \Rightarrow \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{x^3 d x}{x^4\left(x^4+1\right)} d x\begin{aligned} & \text{ Let } x^4=t \Rightarrow 4 x^3=d t \\ & \therefore \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{4} \int \frac{d t}{t(t+1)}=\frac{1}{4} \int\left[\frac{1}{t}-\frac{1}{t+1}\right] d t \\ & =\frac{1}{4}[\log (t)-\log (t+1)]+\mathrm{C}=\frac{1}{4} \log \left(\frac{t}{t+1}\right) \\ & \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{4} \log \left(\frac{x^4}{x^4+1}\right)+\mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $\int \frac{2-\sin x}{2 \cos x+3} d x=$
questions.solution: $\mathrm{I}=\int \frac{2-\sin x}{2 \cos x+3} d x\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{2}{2 \cos x+3} d x+\int \frac{-\sin x}{2 \cos x+3} d x \\ & \mathrm{I}=\mathrm{I}_1+\mathrm{I}_2 \\ & \mathrm{I}_1=\int \frac{2}{2 \cos x+3} d x=2 \int \frac{\sec ^2 \frac{x}{2}}{\tan ^2 \frac{x}{2}+5} d x \\ & \text{ Let } \frac{\tan \frac{x}{2}}{\sqrt{5}}=u \Rightarrow d \mathrm{u}=\frac{\sec ^2\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)}{2 \sqrt{5}} d x \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{I}_1=2 \int \frac{2 \sqrt{5}}{5 u^2+5} d u \\ & \mathrm{I}_1=\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}} \int \frac{1}{u^2+1} d u=\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}} \tan ^{-1} u+\mathrm{C}_1 \\ & \mathrm{I}_1=\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \tan \frac{x}{2}\right)+\mathrm{C}_1 \\ & \mathrm{I}_2=\int \frac{-\sin x}{2 \cos x+3} \qquad [\because \int \frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{f(x)}=\log f(x)+C] \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \log (2 \cos x+3)+\mathrm{C}_2 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{I}=\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \tan \frac{x}{2}\right)+\log \sqrt{2 \cos x+3}+\mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \sin ^{-1} \sqrt{\frac{x}{a+x}} d x=$
questions.solution: $\mathrm{I}=\int \sin ^{-1} \sqrt{\frac{x}{a+x}} d x\begin{aligned} & \text{ Let } x=a \tan ^2 t \Rightarrow d x=2 a \tan t \sec ^2 t d t \\ & \mathrm{I}=\int \sin ^{-1} \sqrt{\frac{a \tan ^2 t}{a+a \tan ^2 t}}\left(2 a \tan t \sec ^2 t\right) d t \\ & =2 a \int \sin ^{-1} \sqrt{\frac{a \tan ^2 t}{a \sec ^2 t}} \tan t \sec ^2 t d t \\ & =2 a \int t\left(\tan \sec ^2 t\right) d t\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =2 a\left[t \int \tan t \sec ^2 t d t-\int \frac{d t}{d t} \int \tan t \sec ^2 t d t\right] \\ & =2 a\left[\frac{t \tan ^2 t}{2}-\int \frac{\tan ^2 t}{2} d t\right] \\ & =a t \tan ^2 t-a \int\left(\sec ^2 t-1\right) d t \\ & =\text{ at } \tan ^2 t-a \tan t+\mathrm{at}+\mathrm{C} \\ & \text{ Put } t=\tan ^{-1} \sqrt{\frac{x}{a}} \\ & \mathrm{I}=a\left[\frac{x}{a} \tan ^{-1} \sqrt{\frac{x}{a}}-\sqrt{\frac{x}{a}}+\tan ^{-1} \sqrt{\frac{x}{a}}\right]+\mathrm{C} \\ & \mathrm{I}=(a+x) \tan ^{-1} \sqrt{\frac{x}{a}}-\sqrt{a x}+\mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\frac{A}{x-a}+\frac{B x+C}{x^2+b^2}=\frac{1}{(x-a)\left(x^2+b^2\right)}$ then $\mathrm{C}=$
questions.solution:
$\frac{A}{(x-a)}+\frac{B x+C}{x^2+b^2}=\frac{1}{(x-a)\left(x^2+b^2\right)}\Rightarrow A\left(x^2+b^2\right)+(B x+C)(x-a)=1\Rightarrow(A+B) x^2+(C-a B) x+A b^2-a C=1$
On comparing we get,
$A+B=0$ ....(i)
$C-a B=0$ ....(ii)
$A b^2-a C=1$ ....(iii)
From (i) and (ii),
$C+a A=0 \Rightarrow A=\frac{-C}{a}$; Put $A=\frac{-C}{a}$ in equation (iii),
$\frac{-C}{a} b^2-a C=1 \Rightarrow-C\left(\frac{b^2+a^2}{a}\right)=1 \Rightarrow C=\frac{-a}{a^2+b^2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
$\int \frac{2 x^2-3}{\left(x^2-4\right)\left(x^2+1\right)} d x=\mathrm{Atan}^{-1} x+\mathrm{B} \log (x-2)+\mathrm{C} \log (x+2)$
then $6 A+7 B-5 C=$
questions.solution: $\int \frac{\left(2 x^2-3\right)}{\left(x^2-4\right)\left(x^2+1\right)} d x=\int \frac{\left(2\left(x^2+1\right)-5\right)}{\left(x^2-4\right)\left(x^2+1\right)} d x=\int \frac{2}{x^2-4} d x-\int\left(\frac{1}{x^2-4}-\frac{1}{x^2+1}\right) d x=\int \frac{1}{x^2-4} d x+\int \frac{1}{x^2+1} d x=\frac{1}{4} \ln \left(\frac{x-2}{x+2}\right)+\tan ^{-1} x=\frac{1}{4} \log (x-2)-\frac{1}{4} \ln (x+2)+\tan ^{-1} xA=1 ; B=\frac{1}{4} ; C=-\frac{1}{4} \Rightarrow 6 A+7 B-5 C=6+\frac{7}{4}+\frac{5}{4}=9$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \frac{3 x^9+7 x^8}{\left(x^2+2 x+5 x^8\right)^2} d x=$
questions.solution:
$I=\int \frac{3 x^9+7 x^8}{\left(x^2+2 x+5 x^8\right)^2} d xI=\int \frac{3 x^9+7 x^8}{x^{16}\left(\frac{1}{x^6}+\frac{2}{x^7}+5\right)^2} d x \Rightarrow I=\int \frac{3 x^{-7}+7 x^{-8}}{\left(\frac{1}{x^6}+\frac{2}{x^7}+5\right)^2} d x$
Let $\frac{1}{x^6}+\frac{2}{x^7}+5=t \Rightarrow\left(-6 x^{-7}-14 x^{-8}\right) d x=d t\therefore I=\frac{-1}{2} \int \frac{1}{t^2} d t \Rightarrow I=\frac{1}{2 t}+C\Rightarrow I=\frac{1}{2\left(\frac{1}{x^6}+\frac{2}{x^7}+5\right)}+C \Rightarrow I=\frac{x^7}{2\left(x+2+5 x^7\right)}+C$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \frac{\cos x+x \sin x}{x(x+\cos x)} d x=$
questions.solution: $I=\int \frac{\cos x+x \sin x}{x(x+\cos x)} d x=\int \frac{\cos x}{x(x+\cos x)} d x+\int \frac{\sin x}{(x+\cos x)} d x=\int\left\{\frac{1}{x}-\frac{1}{x+\cos x}\right\} d x+\int \frac{\sin x}{x+\cos x} d x=\int\left\{\frac{1}{x}-\frac{(1-\sin x}{x+\cos x}\right\} d x=\ln x-\ln (x+\cos x)+C=\ln \left|\frac{x}{x+\cos x}\right|+C$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int \sqrt{\frac{2}{1+\sin x}} d x=2 \log |A(x)-B(x)|+C$ and $0 \leq x \leq \frac{\pi}{2}$ then $B\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=$
questions.solution:
$I=\int \sqrt{\frac{2}{1+\sin x}} d x \Rightarrow I=\int \sqrt{\frac{2}{1+\cos \left(x-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)}} d x$
$I=\int \frac{1}{\cos \left(\frac{x}{2}-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)} d x \Rightarrow I=\int \sec \left(\frac{x}{2}-\frac{\pi}{4}\right) d x$
$I=2 \log \left|\sec \left(\frac{x}{2}-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)+\tan \left(\frac{x}{2}-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right|+C$
$I=2 \log \left|\sec \left(\frac{x}{2}-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)-\tan \left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{x}{2}\right)\right|+C$
$\Rightarrow B(x)=\tan \left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{x}{2}\right) \Rightarrow B\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\tan \left(\frac{\pi}{8}\right)$
Now, $\tan \left(\frac{2 \pi}{8}\right)=\frac{2 \tan \frac{\pi}{8}}{1-\tan ^2 \frac{\pi}{8}} \Rightarrow \tan ^2 \frac{\pi}{8}+2 \tan \frac{\pi}{8}-1=0$
Let $\tan \frac{\pi}{8}=y \Rightarrow y^2+2 y-1=0 \Rightarrow y= \pm \sqrt{2}-1$
$\tan \frac{\pi}{8}\gt0 \Rightarrow \tan \frac{\pi}{8}=\sqrt{2}-1$
$\therefore B\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\sqrt{2}-1=\frac{2-1}{\sqrt{2}+1}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{(\sqrt{2}+1)^2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3+2 \sqrt{2}}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int \frac{3}{2 \cos ^3 x \sqrt{2 \sin 2 x}} d x=\frac{3}{2}(\tan x)^B+\frac{1}{10}(\tan x)^A+c$ then $\mathrm{A}=$
questions.solution: $\frac{3}{2 \cos ^3 x \sqrt{2 \sin 2 x}}=\frac{3}{2 \cos ^3 x \sqrt{\frac{4 \tan x}{1+\tan ^2 x}}}I=\int \frac{3 \sec ^4 x}{4 \sqrt{\tan x}} d x=\int \frac{3}{4} \frac{\left(1+\tan ^2 x\right)}{\sqrt{\tan x}} \sec ^2 x d x\tan x=\mathrm{t} \Rightarrow d t=\sec ^2 x d xI=\frac{3}{4} \int\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}}+t^{3 / 2}\right) d t=\frac{3}{4}\left[2 \sqrt{t}+\frac{2}{5} t^{5 / 2}\right]+C=\frac{3}{4}\left[2 \sqrt{\tan x}+\frac{2}{5}(\tan x)^{5 / 2}\right]+C=\frac{3}{2}(\tan x)^{1 / 2}+\frac{3}{10}(\tan x)^{5 / 2}+C \Rightarrow A=\frac{5}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\frac{1}{x^4+1}=\frac{A x+B}{x^2+\sqrt{2} x+1}+\frac{C x+D}{x^2-\sqrt{2} x+1}$ then $B D-A C=$
questions.solution:
Since, given
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{x^4+1}=\frac{A x+B}{x^2+\sqrt{2} x+1}+\frac{C x+D}{x^2-\sqrt{2} x+1} \\
& \Rightarrow(A x+B)\left(x^2-\sqrt{2} x+1\right)+(C x+D)\left(x^2+\sqrt{2} x+1\right)=1
\end{aligned}$
If $x=0 \Rightarrow B+D=1$
Equating co-efficient of $x^3 \Rightarrow A+C=0$
Equating co-efficient of $x^2 \Rightarrow B-\sqrt{2} A+D+\sqrt{2} C=0\Rightarrow 1+\sqrt{2}(C-A)=0 \Rightarrow A-C=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
Aftersolving A+C=0 and $A-C=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \Rightarrow A=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{2}}, C=\frac{-1}{2 \sqrt{2}}$
Equating co-efficient of $x \Rightarrow A-\sqrt{2} B+C+\sqrt{2} D=0\Rightarrow B-D=0 \Rightarrow B=\frac{1}{2}, D=\frac{1}{2}$
Now, $B D-A C \Rightarrow \frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{8}=\frac{3}{8}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \frac{2 x^2 \cos \left(x^2\right)-\sin \left(x^2\right)}{x^2} d x=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text{ Let } h=\int \frac{2 x^2 \cos \left(x^2\right)-\sin \left(x^2\right)}{x^2} d x \\ = & \int \frac{x \cdot d\left(\sin \left(x^2\right)\right)-\sin \left(x^2\right) \cdot d(x)}{x^2} \\ = & \int d\left(\frac{\sin \left(x^2\right)}{x}\right)=\frac{\sin \left(x^2\right)}{x}+c.\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int \frac{\log \left(1+x^4\right)}{x^3} d x=f(x) \log \left(\frac{1}{g(x)}\right)+\tan ^{-1}(h(x))+c$, then $h(x)\left[f(x)+f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\right]=$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{ Given, } \int \frac{\log \left(1+x^4\right)}{x^3} d x \\
= & f(x) \log \left(\frac{1}{g(x)}\right)+\tan ^{-1}(h(x))+c \\
\Rightarrow & \int x^{-3} \log \left(1+x^4\right) d x \\
= & \log \left(1+x^4\right) \cdot \frac{x^{-2}}{-2}+\frac{1}{2} \int\left(\frac{4 x^3}{1+x^4} \cdot x^{-2}\right) d x \\
= & -\frac{1}{2 x^2} \log \left(1+x^4\right)+\int \frac{2 x}{1+x^4} d x
\end{aligned}$
Let $x^2=t \Rightarrow 2 x=\mathrm{dt}=-\frac{1}{2 x^2} \log \left(1+x^4\right)+\int \frac{d t}{1+t^2}\begin{aligned} & =-\frac{1}{2 x^2} \log \left(1+x^4\right)+\tan ^{-1}\left(x^2\right)+c \\ & \text{ So } f(x)=\frac{1}{2 x^2}, g(x)=1+x^4, h(x)=x^2 \\ & =x^2\left(\frac{1}{2 x^2}+\frac{x^2}{2}\right)=\frac{1+x^4}{2}=\frac{g(x)}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $f(x)=\int \frac{x}{  \left(x^2+1\right)\left(x^2+3\right)} d x$. If f(3)=$\frac{1}{4} \log\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)$ then $f(0)=$
questions.solution:
$\because f(x)=\int \frac{x}{\left(x^2+1\right)\left(x^2+3\right)} d x$
Let $x^2=t \Rightarrow 2 x d x=d t\begin{aligned}
& \text{ So, } f(x)=\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{d t}{(t+1)(t+3)} \\
& =\frac{1}{4} \int\left(\frac{1}{t+1}-\frac{1}{t+3}\right) d t=\frac{1}{4} \log \left(\frac{1+x^2}{3+x^2}\right)+c
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text{ Since, } f(3)=\frac{1}{4} \log \left(\frac{5}{6}\right) \Rightarrow \frac{1}{4} \log \left(\frac{5}{6}\right) \\ & =\frac{1}{4} \log \left(\frac{10}{12}\right)+c \Rightarrow c=0 \\ & \Rightarrow f(x)=\frac{1}{4} \log \left(\frac{1+x^2}{3+x^2}\right) \text{ So, } f(0)=\frac{1}{4} \log \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \frac{2 \cos 2 x}{(1+\sin 2 x)(1+\cos 2 x)} d x=$
questions.solution: $I=\int \frac{2 \cos 2 x}{(1+\sin 2 x)(1+\cos 2 x)} d x\begin{aligned} & =2 \int \frac{\frac{1-\tan ^2 x}{1+\tan ^2 x}}{\left(1+\frac{2 \tan x}{1+\tan ^2 x}\right)\left(1+\frac{1-\tan ^2 x}{1+\tan ^2 x}\right)} d x \\ & =\int \frac{(1-\tan x) \sec ^2 x}{(1+\tan x)} d x \cdot \text{ Let } \tan x=t \Rightarrow \sec ^2 x d x=d t \\ & =\int\left(\frac{1-t}{1+t}\right) d t=\int\left(-1+\frac{2}{1+t}\right) d t \\ & =-\tan x+2 \log (1+\tan x)+c.\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int\left(\frac{x}{x \cos x-\sin x}\right)^2 d x=$
questions.solution: Let $I=\int\left(\frac{x}{x \cos x-\sin x}\right)^2 d x\begin{aligned} & =\int \frac{x^2}{(x \cos x-\sin x)^2} d x \\ & =-\int \frac{x}{\sin x} \times \frac{(-x \sin x)}{(x \cos x-\sin x)^2} d x \\ & =\frac{-x}{\sin x} \times \frac{(-1)}{(x \cos x-\sin x)}-\int \frac{\sin x-x \cos x}{\sin ^2 x(x \cos x-\sin x)} d x \\ & =\frac{x}{\sin x(x \cos x-\sin x)}+\int \operatorname{cosec}^2 x d x \\ & =\frac{x \operatorname{cosec} x}{x \cos x-\sin x}-\cot x+c.\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{n}}=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \tan ^n x d x$, then $\mathrm{I}_{13}+\mathrm{I}_{11}=$
questions.solution:
Given, $I_n=\int_0^{\pi / 4} \tan ^n x d x$
and $I_{n+1}=\int_0^{\pi / 4} \tan ^{n+1} x d x \quad(n \rightarrow n+1)I_{n-1}=\int_0^{\pi / 4} \tan ^{n-1} x d x \quad(n \rightarrow n-1)$
Since, we know $I_{n-1}+I_{n+1}=\frac{1}{n} \Rightarrow I_{11}+I_{13}=\frac{1}{12} \quad(\because n=12)$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \frac{1}{x^5 \sqrt[5]{x^5+1}} d x=$
questions.solution:
Let, $\mathrm{I}=\int \frac{1}{x^5 \sqrt[5]{x^5+1}} d x=\int \frac{1}{1^{\frac{1}{5}}} d xx^6\left(1+\frac{1}{x^5}\right)^{\overline{5}}$
Let $1+\frac{1}{x^5}=t \Rightarrow \frac{1}{x^6} d x=-\frac{1}{5} d t$
Now, $\mathrm{I}=\frac{-1}{5} \int \frac{1}{t^{\frac{1}{5}}} d t=-\frac{1}{5} \int t^{\frac{-1}{5}} d t=\frac{-1}{5} \cdot \frac{t^{\frac{4}{5}}}{\frac{4}{5}}+\mathrm{C}=\frac{-1}{4} t^{\frac{4}{5}}+\mathrm{C}=-\frac{1}{4}\left(1+\frac{1}{x^5}\right)^{\frac{4}{5}}+\mathrm{C}=\frac{-\left(1+x^5\right)^5}{4 x^4}+\mathrm{C}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \frac{x+1}{\sqrt{x^2+x+1}} d x=$
questions.solution:
Let, $\mathrm{I}=\int \frac{x+1}{\sqrt{x^2+x+1}} d x\begin{aligned} & =\int \frac{2 x+1+1}{2 \sqrt{x^2+x+1}} d x \\ & =\int \frac{2 x+1}{2 \sqrt{x^2+x+1}} d x+\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{x^2+x+1}} d x\end{aligned}=\mathrm{I}_1+\mathrm{I}_2$
Now, $\mathrm{I}_1=\int \frac{2 x+1}{2 \sqrt{x^2+x+1}} d x$, Let $x^2+x+1=t\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow(2 x+1) d x=d t \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{I}_1=\int \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{t}} d t=\sqrt{t}+\mathrm{C}_1=\sqrt{x^2+x+1}+\mathrm{C}_1\end{aligned}$ and $\mathrm{I}_2=\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2}} d x=\frac{1}{2} \sinh ^{-1}\left(\frac{x+\frac{1}{2}}{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}\right)+\mathrm{C}_2=\frac{1}{2} \sinh ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x+1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)+\mathrm{C}_2$
So, $\mathrm{I}=\sqrt{x^2+x+1}+\frac{1}{2} \sinh ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x+1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)+\mathrm{C} \quad\left\{\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}_1+\mathrm{C}_2\right\}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int\left(\tan ^7 x+\tan x\right) d x=$
questions.solution: Let $\mathrm{I}=\int\left(\tan ^7 x+\tan x\right) d x\begin{aligned} & =\int\left(\tan ^5 x\left(\sec ^2 x-1\right)+\tan x\right) d x \\ & =\int\left\{\tan ^5 x \sec ^2 x-\tan ^3 x\left(\sec ^2 x-1\right)+\tan x\right\} d x\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}=\int\left\{\tan ^5 x \sec ^2 x-\tan ^3 x \sec ^2 x+\tan x\left(\sec ^2 x-1\right)\right.\end{aligned}+\tan x\} d x\begin{aligned} & =\int\left\{\tan ^5 x \sec ^2 x-\tan ^3 x \cdot \sec ^2 x+\tan x \sec ^2 x\right\} d x \\ & =\int\left(\tan ^5 x-\tan ^3 x+\tan x\right) \sec ^2 x d x\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text{ Let } \tan x=t \Rightarrow \sec ^2 x d x=d t \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{I}=\int\left(t^5-t^3+t\right) d t\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{t^6}{6}-\frac{t^4}{4}+\frac{t^2}{2}+\mathrm{C}=\frac{t^2}{12}\left(2 t^4-3 t^2+6\right)+\mathrm{C} \\ & =\frac{\tan ^2 x}{12}\left(2 \tan ^4 x-3 \tan ^2 x+6\right)+\mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \frac{\operatorname{cosec} x}{3 \cos x+4 \sin x} d x=$
questions.solution: Let $\mathrm{I}=\int \frac{\operatorname{cosec} x}{3 \cos x+4 \sin x} d x=\int \frac{\operatorname{cosec}^2 x}{3 \cot x+4} d x$, Let $3 \cot x+4=t\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow-3 \operatorname{cosec}^2 x d x=d t \\ & =\frac{-1}{3} \int \frac{1}{t} d t=-\frac{1}{3} \log |t|+\mathrm{C}\end{aligned}=\frac{-1}{3} \log |3 \cot x+4|+C=-\frac{1}{3} \log \left|\frac{3 \cos x+4 \sin x}{\sin x}\right|+\mathrm{C}=\frac{1}{3} \log \left|\frac{\sin x}{3 \cos x+4 \sin x}\right|+C$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int e^{2 x+3} \sin 6 x d x=$
questions.solution: Let $\mathrm{I}=\int e^{2 x+3} \sin 6 x d x=\sin 6 x \frac{e^{2 x+3}}{2}-\int\left(6 \cos 6 x \cdot \frac{e^{2 x+3}}{2}\right) d x=\frac{e^{2 x+3}}{2} \sin 6 x-3 \int e^{2 x+3} \cos 6 x d x=\frac{e^{2 x+3}}{2} \sin 6 x-3\left\{\cos 6 x. \frac{e^{2 x}+3}{2}+\int 6 \sin 6 x. \frac{e^{2 x+3}}{2} d x\right\}=\frac{e^{2 x+3}}{2} \sin 6 x-\frac{3}{2} e^{2 x+3} \cos 6 x-91\Rightarrow 10 \mathrm{I}=\frac{e^{2 x+3}}{2}(\sin 6 x-3 \cos 6 x)+C\Rightarrow \mathrm{I}=\frac{e^{2 x+3}}{20}(\sin 6 x-3 \cos 6 x)+C$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(x)=\frac{x}{\left(1+n x^n\right)^{1 / n}}$ for $n \geq 2$, then $\int x^{n-2} f(x) d x=$
questions.solution:
$\int x^{n-2} f(x) d x=\int \frac{x^{n-1}}{\left(1+n x^n\right)^{1 / n}} d x$

Let $1+n x n=\mathrm{t} \Rightarrow x^{n-1} d x=\frac{1}{n^2} d t \begin{aligned}$& =$\frac{1}{n^2} \int \frac{d t}{t^{1 / n}}=\frac{1}{n^2} \frac{t^{-1 / n}+1}{\left(-\frac{1}{n}+1\right)}+$C \\
& =$\frac{1}{n(n-1)}\left(1+n x^n\right)^{1-\frac{1}{n}}+C
\end{aligned}
$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \frac{1+x \cos x}{x\left[1-x^2\left(e^{\sin x}\right)^2\right]} d x=$
questions.solution:
$$\begin{aligned}& \text{ Let } \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{(1+x \cos x)}{x\left[1-x^2\left(e^{\sin x}\right)^2\right]}\\
& d x=\int \frac{(1+x \cos x) e^{\sin x}}{x e^{\sin x}\left[1-\left(x e^{\sin x}\right)^2\right]}d x
\end{aligned}$$

Let $ x e^{\sin } x=t \Rightarrow e^{\sin x} \cdot(1+x \cos x) d x=d t
\begin{aligned}& \text{ Hence } I=\int \frac{d t}{t   \left(1-t²\right)}=\int\left[\ffrac{1}{t}-\frac{1}{2(t-1)}-\frac{1}{2(t+1)}\right]d t \\
& \Rightarrow \quad I=\ln |\mathrm{t}|-\frac{1}{2} \ln |(\mathrm{t}-1)|-\frac{1}{2} \ln |(\mathrm{t}+1)|+C \\
& =\frac{1}{2} \ln \left|\frac{\left(x e^{\sin x}\right)^2}{\left(x e^{\sin x}\right)^2-1}\right|+C
\end{aligned}
$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \frac{d x}{(x-1) \sqrt{x+2}}=$
questions.solution: Let $I=\int \frac{d x}{(x-1) \sqrt{x+2}}$ Let $x=t^2-2$ or $t=\sqrt{x+2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{d} x=2 t d t$ Hence $I=\int \frac{2 t d t}{\left(\mathrm{t}^2-3\right) \mathrm{t}}=\frac{2}{2 \sqrt{3}} \log \left|\frac{t-\sqrt{3}}{t+\sqrt{3}}\right|+C=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \log \left|\frac{\sqrt{x+2}-\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{x+2}+\sqrt{3}}\right|+C$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int e^{-2 x}\left(\frac{1-\sin 2 x}{1+\cos 2 x}\right) d x=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text{ Let } I \int e\left(\frac{1 \sin 2}{1 \cos 2}\right) d x \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \int e^{-2 x}\left(\sec ^2 x-2 \tan x\right) d x \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \int e^{-2 x} \cdot \sec ^2 x d x-\int e^{-2 x} \tan x d x \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[e^{-2 x} \cdot \tan x+2 \int e^{-2 x} \tan x d x\right]-\int e^{-2 x} \cdot \tan x d x \\ & =\frac{1}{2} e^{-2 x} \cdot \tan x+C\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\frac{x^2-7 x+2}{x^4+3 x^2+4}=\frac{A x+B}{x^2+a x+2}+\frac{C x+D}{x^2+b x+2}$ and $a > b$ then $\mathrm{B}+\mathrm{D}=$
questions.solution:
$\frac{x^2-7 x+2}{x^4+3 x^2+4}=\frac{A x+B}{x^2+a x+2}+\frac{C x+D}{x^2+b x+2}$ ...(i)
$\because \frac{x^2-7 x+2}{x^4+3 x^2+4}=\frac{x^2-7 x+2}{\left(x^2+x+2\right)\left(x^2-x+2\right)}$
The form of the partial fraction decomposition is :$\frac{x^2-7 x+2}{\left(-x^2-x+2\right)\left(x^2+x+2\right)}=\frac{P x+Q}{x^2-x+2}+\frac{R x+S}{x^2+x+2}$ ...(ii)
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow x^2-7 x+2=(P x+Q)\left(x^2+x+2\right)+(R x+S) \\ & \left(x^2-x+2\right) \\ & \Rightarrow x^2-7 x+2=x^3(P+R)+x^2(-P+Q+R+S)+x(2 P \\ & -Q+2 R+S)+(2 Q+2 S)\end{aligned}$
So, by comparing both sides, we get:
$\begin{aligned} & P+R=0 \\ & -P+Q+R+S=1\end{aligned}2 P-Q+2 R+S=-72 \mathrm{Q}+2 \mathrm{ S}=2$ ...(iii)
Solving system (iii), we get:
$P=0, Q=4, R=0 S=-3\therefore \frac{x^2-7 x+2}{x^4+3 x^2+4}=\frac{4}{x^2+x+2}+\frac{-3}{x^2-x+2}$ ...(iv)
From $\mathrm{eq}^{\mathrm{n}}(\mathrm{i}) \ \text{ and } $ (iv):
$\begin{aligned} & A=0, B=4, C=0, D=-3 \\ & a=1, b=-1 \\ & B+D=4-3=1 \\ & 2 a+b=2-1=1\end{aligned}\therefore B+D=2 a+b$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \frac{d x}{\sin (x-a) \cos (x-b)}=$
questions.solution: $\int \frac{d x}{\sin (x-a) \cos (x-b)}=\frac{1}{\cos (b-a)} \int \frac{\cos [(x-a)-(x-b)]}{\sin (x-a) \cos (x-b)}=\frac{1}{\cos (b-a)}\int\left[\frac{\cos (x-a) \cos (x-b)+\sin (x-a) \sin (x-b)}{\sin (x-a) \cos (x-b)}\right] d x\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{\cos (b+a)} \int\left[\frac{\cos (x-a)}{\sin (x-a)}+\frac{\sin (x-b)}{\cos (x-b)}\right] d x \\ & =\frac{1}{\cos (b-a)} \quad[\log (\sin (x-a)-\log (\cos (x-b))]+C \\ & =\frac{1}{\cos (b-a)} \log \left|\frac{\sin (x-a)}{\operatorname{cós}(x-b)}\right|+C\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $I_n=\int \tan ^n x d x(n > 1)$, then $I_4+I_6=$
questions.solution:
$\int \tan ^n x d x\begin{aligned} & I_4+I_6=\int \tan ^4 x d x+\int \tan ^6 x d x \\ & =\int\left(\tan ^4 x+\tan ^6 x\right) d x=\int \tan ^4 x \sec ^2 x d x\end{aligned}$
Let $\tan x=t \Rightarrow \sec ^2 x d x=d t\therefore \quad \mathrm{I}_4+\mathrm{I}_6=\int \mathrm{t}^4 \mathrm{dt}=\frac{\mathrm{t}^5}{5}+\mathrm{C}\mathrm{I}_4+\mathrm{I}_6=\frac{1}{5} \tan ^5 \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{C}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int \sqrt{x}\left(1-x^3\right)^{\frac{-1}{2}} d x=\frac{2}{3} g(f(x))+c$, then
questions.solution:
$I=\int \sqrt{x}\left(1-x^3\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}} d x$
Let $\mathrmx^{\frac{3}{2}}=\mathrm{t} \Rightarrow \frac{3}{2} \mathrmx^{\frac{1}{2}} \mathrm{dx}=\mathrm{dt} \Rightarrow \sqrt{\mathrm{x}} \mathrm{dx}=\frac{2}{3} \mathrm{dt}\therefore \mathrm{I}=\int\left(1-\mathrm{t}^2\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{2}{3} \mathrm{dt}=\frac{2}{3} \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-\mathrm{t}^2}} \mathrm{dt}\begin{aligned} & I=\frac{2}{3} \sin ^{-1} t+c \\ & I=\frac{2}{3} \sin ^{-1}\left(x^{\frac{3}{2}}\right)+c\end{aligned}$
Let $f(x)=x^{3 / 2} \ \text{$ and $} g(x)=\sin ^{-1} x$ Then, $I=\frac{2}{3} g(f(x))+c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \frac{x^2}{\left(x^2-1\right)\left(x^2+1\right)} d x=$
questions.solution: Let $\int \frac{x^2}{\left(x^2-1\right)\left(x^2+1\right)} d x=I\Rightarrow I=\frac{1}{2} \int\left(\frac{1}{x^2-1}+\frac{1}{x^2+1}\right) d x\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2} \ln \left|\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right|+\frac{1}{2} \tan ^{-1} x+c \\ & =\frac{1}{4} \ln \left|\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right|+\frac{1}{2} \tan ^{-1} x+c\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\frac{d}{d x}\left(\frac{x^2}{(x+2)(2 x+3)}\right)=\frac{A}{(x+2)^2}+\frac{B}{(2 x+3)^2}$ then $\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}=$
questions.solution:
$\because \frac{d}{d x}\left(\frac{x^2}{(x+2)(2 x+3)}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{A}}{(x+2)^2}+\frac{\mathrm{B}}{(2 x+3)^2}\Rightarrow\left(\frac{7 x^2+12 x}{(x+2)(2 x+3)}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{A}}{(x+2)^2}+\frac{\mathrm{B}}{(2 x+3)^2}$ ...(i)
The form of the partial fraction decomposition is
$\frac{7 x^2+12 x}{(x+2)^2(2 x+3)^2}=\frac{\mathrm{A}}{x+2}+\frac{\mathrm{B}}{(x+2)^2}+\frac{\mathrm{C}}{(2 x+3)}+\frac{\mathrm{D}}{(2 x+3)^2}$ ...(ii)
$\begin{array}{r}\Rightarrow 7 x^2+12 x=\mathrm{A}(x+2)(2 x+3)^2+\mathrm{B}(2 x+3)^2+ \\ \mathrm{C}(x+2)^2(2 x+3)+\mathrm{D}(x+2)^2\end{array} \begin{aligned}$& \Rightarrow 7 x²+12 x=x³(4 $\mathrm{ A}+2 \mathrm{C})+$ x^2(20 $\mathrm{ A}+4 \mathrm{ B}+11 \mathrm{C}+\mathrm{D})+$\\ & x(33 $\mathrm{ A}+12 \mathrm{ B}+20 \mathrm{C}+4 \mathrm{D})+18 \mathrm{ A}+9 \mathrm{ B}+12 \mathrm{C}+4 \mathrm{D}\end{aligned}
Comparing the coefficients, we get: \begin{aligned}$& 4 A+2 C=0 \\ & 20 A+4 B+11 C+D=7\end{aligned}33 $\mathrm{ A}+12 \mathrm{ B}+20 \mathrm{C}+4 \mathrm{D}=12$ ...(iii)
$18 \mathrm{ A}+9 \mathrm{ B}+12 \mathrm{C}+4 \mathrm{D}=0$
Solving above system of equation, we get $A=0, B=4, C=0, D=-9\begin{aligned} \text{ and } \therefore \frac{7 x^2+12 x}{(x+2)^2(2 x+3)^2}=\frac{4}{(x+2)^2}-\frac{9}{(2 x+3)^2}$\\ & \therefore $\frac{d}{d x}\left(\frac{x^2}{(x+2)(2 x+3)}\right)=\frac{4}{(x+2)^2}+\frac{(-9)}{(2 x+3)^2}\end{aligned}
From \mathrm{eq}^{\mathrm{n}} (i)
$ A=4, B=-9 \Rightarrow A+B=4-9=-5

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \frac{d x}{\left(2 a x+x^2\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}=$
questions.solution:
Let $\mathrm{I}=\int \frac{d x}{\left(2 a x+x^2\right)^{3 / 2}}=\int \frac{d x}{\left((x+a)^2-a^2\right)^{3 / 2}}$
Let $t=x+a \Rightarrow d t=d x\Rightarrow \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{d t}{\left(t^2-a^2\right)^{3 / 7}}$
Put $t=a \sec p\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{d t}{d p}=a \sec p \tan p \Rightarrow d t=a \sec p \tan p d p \\ & \therefore \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{a \sec p \tan p}{\left(a^2 \sec 2 p-a^2\right)^{3 / 2}} d p \\ & =\frac{1}{a^2} \int \frac{\sec p \tan p}{\left(\tan ^2 p\right)^{3 / 2}} d p=\frac{1}{a^2} \int \frac{\cos p}{\sin ^2 p} d p \\ & =-\frac{1}{a^2}\left(\frac{1}{\sin p}\right)+c=-\frac{1}{a^2}\left(\frac{1}{\sin \left(\sec ^{-1} \frac{t}{a}\right)}\right)+c \\ & =-\frac{1}{a^2}\left(\frac{1}{\left(\frac{(a) \sqrt{\frac{t^2}{a^2}}-1}{t}\right)+c=-\frac{1}{a^3}\left(\frac{t}{\sqrt{\frac{t^2}{a^2}-1}}\right)+c}\right. \\ & =-\frac{1}{a^3}\left(\frac{x+a}{\sqrt{\frac{(\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{a})^2}{a^2}-1}}\right)+c=-\frac{1}{a^2}\left(\frac{x+a}{\sqrt{x^2+2 a x}}\right)+c\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \frac{1-\cos x}{\cos x(1+\cos x)} d x=$
questions.solution: $\int \frac{1-\cos x}{\cos x(1+\cos x)} d x=\int \frac{1+\cos x-2 \cos x}{\cos x(1+\cos x)} d x\begin{aligned} & =\int \frac{1}{\cos x} d x-2 \int \frac{1}{1+\cos x} d x \\ & =\int \sec x d x-2 \int \frac{1}{1+\cos x} d x \\ & =\int \sec x d x-2 \int \frac{1-\cos x}{1-\cos ^2 x} d x \\ & =\int \sec x d x-2 \int\left(\operatorname{cosec}^2 x-\cot x \cdot \operatorname{cosec} x\right) d x \\ & =\log |\sec x+\tan x|-2[\operatorname{cosec} x-\cot x]+\mathrm{c}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $g(x)$ is an anti derivative of $f(x)=1+2^x \log 2$ and the graph of $y=g(x)$ passes through $\left(-1, \frac{1}{2}\right)$. Then the curve meets the $\mathrm{Y}$ - axis at
questions.solution:
$f(x)=1+2^x \log 2\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \int f(x)=\int\left(1+2^x \log 2\right) d x \\ & \Rightarrow g(x)=x+\frac{2^x \log 2}{\log 2}+c\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \mathrm{g}(x)=x+2^x+c \Rightarrow y=x+2^x+c$  ...(i)
Equation (i) passes through $\left(-1, \frac{1}{2}\right)\therefore \frac{1}{2}=-1+2^{-1}+c \Rightarrow c=1$
Putting value of $c in \mathrm{eq}^{\mathrm{n}}$ (i), we get
$y=x+2^x+1$  ...(ii)
When curve (ii) meets $y$-axis: $x=0\therefore y=0+2^{{}^{\circ}}+1=2\therefore$ Curve meet $y$-axis at the point $(0,2)$

$=\frac{1}{16}\left[4 x-\frac{5 x^2}{2}+3 \ln x\right]_1^2=\frac{6 \ln 2-7}{32}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int e^{\sin x} \frac{\left(x \cos ^3 x-\sin x\right)}{\cos ^2 x} d x=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \quad I=\int e^{\sin x}\left(\frac{x \cos ^3 x-\sin x}{\cos ^2 x}\right) d x \\ & =\int e^{\sin x}(x \cos x-\tan x \sec x) d x \\ & =\int e^{\sin x} x \cdot \cos x d x-\int e^{\sin x} \cdot \sec x \tan x d x \\ & =x \int e^{\sin x} \cos x d x-\int\left(1 \cdot \int e^{\sin x} \cos x d x\right) d x- \\ & \left\{e^{\sin x} \int \sec x \tan d x-\int e^{\sin x} \cdot \cos x \int(\sec x \tan x d x) d x\right\}+C \\ & =x e^{\sin x}-\int e^{\sin x} d x-e^{\sin x} \sec x+\int e^{\sin x} d x+C \\ & e^{\sin x}(x-\sec x)+C\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int f(x) d x=\psi(x)$, then $\int x^5 f\left(x^3\right) d x=$
questions.solution:
$\int f(\mathrm{x}) \mathrm{dx}=\psi(\mathrm{x})$
Let $\mathrm{I}=\int x^5 f\left(x^3\right) d x=\int x^3 f\left(x^3\right) x^2 d x$
Let $x^3=t \Rightarrow 3 x^2 d x=d t \Rightarrow x^2 d x=\frac{d t}{3}\therefore \mathrm{I}=\int t f(\mathrm{t}) \cdot \frac{d t}{3}=\frac{1}{3} \int t f(t) \mathrm{dt}=\frac{1}{3}\left[t \cdot \int f(t) \cdot d t-1 \cdot \int f(t) \cdot d t\right]\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{3}\left[t \psi(t)-\int \psi(t) d t\right]+c \\ & =\frac{1}{3} x^3 \psi\left(x^3\right)-\frac{1}{3} \int \psi\left(x^3\right) \cdot 3 x^2 d x \\ & =\frac{1}{3} x^3 \psi\left(x^3\right)-\int x^2 \psi\left(x^3\right) d x\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int \frac{\sin ^2 \alpha-\sin ^2 x}{\cos x-\cos \alpha} d x=f(x)+A x+B$ and $B \in \mathbb{R}$, then
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int \frac{\sin ^2 \alpha-\sin ^2 x}{\cos x-\cos \alpha} d x=\int \frac{\cos ^2 x-\cos ^2 \alpha}{\cos x-\cos \alpha} d x \\ & =\int \cos x+\cos \alpha d x \\ & =\sin x+x \cos \alpha+c \\ & \therefore f(x)=\sin x \& A=\cos \alpha\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int\left(x^{3 m}+x^{2 m}+x^m\right)\left(2 x^{2 m}+3 x^m+6\right)^{\frac{1}{m}} d x=$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{Let } \mathrm{I}=\int\left(x^{3 x}+x^{2 m}+x^m\right)\left(2 x^{2 m}+3 x m+6\right)^{\frac{1}{m}} d x \\
& =\int\left(x^{3 m}+x^{2 m}+x^m\right)\left(\left(2 x^{2 m}+3 x^m+6\right) \frac{x^m}{x^m}\right)^{\frac{1}{m}} d x \\
& =\int\left(x^{3 m-1}+x^{2 m-1}+x^{m-1}\right)\left(2 x^{2 m}+3 x^{2 m}+6 x^m\right)^{\frac{1}{m}} d x
\end{aligned}$
Put $2 x^{2 m}+3 x^{2 m}+6 x^m=t\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow\left(6 m x^{3 m-1}+6 m x^{2 m-1}+6 m x^{m-1}\right) d x=d t \\
& \Rightarrow\left(x^{3 m-1}+x^{2 m-1}+x^{m-1}\right) d x=\frac{d t}{6 m} \\
& \therefore \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{6 m} \int t^{\frac{1}{m}} d t=\frac{1}{6 m} \cdot \frac{t^{\frac{1}{m}}+1}{\left(\frac{1}{m}+1\right)}+c \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{I}=\frac{\left(2 x^{3 m}+3 x^{2 m}+6 x^m\right)}{6(m+1)}+c
\end{aligned}$

\begin{aligned}
& \frac{-x^2+6 x+1}{(x-1)^2\left(x^2+2\right)}=\frac{A}{(x-1)}+\frac{B}{(x-1)^2}+\frac{C x-3}{x^2+2} \\
& \Rightarrow A(x-1)\left(x^2+2\right)+B\left(x^2+2\right)+(C x-3) \times \\
& (x-1)^2=-x^2+6 x+1 \\
& \text{ If } x=1 \Rightarrow 3 B=6 \Rightarrow B=2 \\
& \text{$ and $} A+C=0 \\
& \text{ Now, } A+B+C=2
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $\begin{aligned} & \text{ If } \int \frac{3 x+2}{4 x^2+4 x+5} d x=A \log \left(4 x^2+4 x+5\right)+B \operatorname{Tan}^{-1} \\ & \left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)+C, \text{ then }(A, B)=\end{aligned}$
questions.solution: Let $I=\int \frac{3 x+2}{4 x^2+4 x+5} d x\begin{aligned} & =\frac{3}{8} \int \frac{8 x+4}{4 x^2+4 x+5} d x+\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{1}{4 x^2+4 x+5} d x \\ & =\frac{3}{8} \log \left(4 x^2+4 x+5\right)+\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{1}{(2 x+1)^2+2^2} d x \\ & =\frac{3}{8} \log \left(4 x^2+4 x+5\right)+\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{4} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x+1}{2}\right)+C \\ & =\frac{3}{8} \log \left(4 x^2+4 x+5\right)+\frac{1}{8} \tan ^{-1}\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)+C\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int \frac{\sqrt{x^4+x^{-4}+2}}{x^3} d x=$
questions.solution: Let $I=\int \frac{\sqrt{x^4+x^{-4}+2}}{x^3} d x\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow I=\int \frac{\sqrt{\left(x^2\right)^2+\left(x^{-2}\right)^2+2 x^2 x^{-2}}}{x^3} d x \\ & =\int\left(\frac{x^2+x^{-2}}{x^3}\right) d x=\int\left(\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{x^5}\right) d x \\ & =\ln |x|-\frac{1}{4 x^4}+C\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\int \frac{x^2-1}{x^3 \sqrt{2 x^4-2 x^2+1}} d x=\int \frac{\frac{x^2-1}{x^5}}{\frac{x^3 \sqrt{2 x^4-2 x^2+1}}{x^5}} d x=\int \frac{\frac{1}{x^3}-\frac{1}{x^5}}{\sqrt{2-\frac{2}{x^2}+\frac{1}{x^4}}} d x$...(i)
Let $2-\frac{2}{x^2}+\frac{1}{x^4}=t \Rightarrow\left(0+\frac{4}{x^3}-\frac{4}{x^5}\right) d x=d t\Rightarrow\left(\frac{1}{x^3}-\frac{1}{x^5}\right) d x=\frac{d t}{4}$
Substituting above values in equation (i), we get
$\int \frac{x^2-1}{x^3 \sqrt{2 x^4-2 x^2+1}} d x=\int \frac{d t}{4 \sqrt{t}}=\frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{t^{1 / 2}}{\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)}+C=\frac{1}{2}\left(2-\frac{2}{x^2}+\frac{1}{x^4}\right)^{1 / 2}+C=\frac{1}{2 x^2} \sqrt{2 x^4-2 x^2+1}+C$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the graph of the anti derivative $g(x)$ of $f(x)=\log (\logx)+(\log x)^{-2}$ passes through $(e, 2023-e)$ and the term independent of $x$ in $g(x)$ is $k$, then the sum of all the digits of $\mathrm{k}$ is
questions.solution:
Given : $f(x)=\log (\log x)+(\log x)^{-2}$
Anti-derivative of
$f(x)=\int\left(\log (\log x)+(\log x)^{-2}\right) d x$...(i)
Let $t=\log x \Rightarrow x=e^t\Rightarrow d x=e^t d t$
Using above values in eqn. (i), we get :
Anti-derivative of $f(x)=\int e^t\left(\log t+t^{-2}\right) d t\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad g(x)=\int e^t\left(\log t+t^{-1}-t^{-1}+t^{-2}\right) d t \\ & \Rightarrow \quad g(x)=\int e^t\left(\log t+t^{-1}\right) d t+\int e^t\left(-t^{-1}+t^{-2}\right) d t \\ & =e^t \log t-e^t \cdot t^{-1}+C \\ & =e^t\left(\log t-t^{-1}\right)+C\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad g(x)=e^{(\log x)}\left(\log (\log x)-(\log x)^{-1}\right)+C$...(i)
$\because \quad$ Equation (i) passes through $(e, 2023-e)\therefore \quad$ Eqn. (i) reduces to :
$2023-e=e^{(\log e)}\left(\log (\log e)-(\log e)^{-1}\right)+C\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad 2023-e=e(\log (1)-1)+C \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 2023-e=-e+C \Rightarrow C=2023\end{aligned}$
Putting the value of $C$ in eqn. (i) :
$g(x)=e^{(\log x)}\left(\log (\log x)-(\log x)^{-1}\right)+2023\therefore \quad$ Sum of digits of independent term $=2+0+2+3=7$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(x)=\int \frac{5 x^8+7 x^6}{\left(x^2+2 x^7+1\right)^2} d x(x \geq 0)$ and $f(0)=0$, then the value of $f(1)=$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{Given } f(x)=\int \frac{5 x^8+7 x^6}{\left(x^2+2 x^7+1\right)^2} d x \\
& \Rightarrow f(x)=\int \frac{5 x^{-6}+7 x^{-8}}{\left(\frac{1}{x^7}+\frac{1}{x^5}+2\right)^2}=\frac{1}{2+\frac{1}{x^7}+\frac{1}{x^5}}+c
\end{aligned}$
Since,
$f(0)=0 \Rightarrow c=0 \Rightarrow f(1)=\frac{1}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \frac{\cos ^2 x}{\cos ^2 x+4 \sin ^2 x} d x=$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{Let } I=\int \frac{\cos ^2 x}{\cos ^2 x+4 \sin ^2 x} d x \\
& =\int \frac{\cos ^2 x}{3 \sin ^2 x+1} d x=\int \frac{\sec ^2 x}{\left(\tan ^2 x+1\right)\left(4 \tan ^2 x+1\right)} d x
\end{aligned}$
Let $u=\tan x \Rightarrow d u=\sec ^2 x d x\begin{aligned}
& I=\int \frac{d u}{\left(u^2+1\right)\left(4 u^2+1\right)}=\int\left(\frac{4 / 3}{4 u^2+1}-\frac{1 / 3}{u^2+1}\right) d u \\
& \frac{2}{3} \tan ^{-1}(2 u)-\frac{1}{3} \tan ^{-1}(u)+c
\end{aligned}$
Now $\int_0^{\pi / 4} \frac{\cos ^2 x}{\cos ^2 x+4 \sin ^2 x} d x=\frac{2}{3} \tan ^{-1}(2)-\frac{\pi}{12}$

questions.q: $\int x^3(\log x)^2 d x=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text{Let } I=\int x^3(\log x)^2 d x \\ & =(\log x)^2 \cdot \frac{x^4}{4}-\int \frac{2}{4}(\log x) \cdot x^3 d x \\ & =(\log x)^2 \cdot \frac{x^4}{4}-\frac{1}{2}\left[(\log x) \cdot \frac{x^4}{4}-\int \frac{x^3}{4} d x\right] \\ & =(\log x)^2 \frac{x^4}{4}-\frac{1}{2}\left[(\log x) \frac{x^4}{4}-\frac{x^4}{16}\right]+c\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int \frac{1}{x\left[(\log x)^2+4 \log x-1\right]} d x=A \log \left[\frac{\log x+B}{\log x+C}\right]+K$ where $\mathrm{K}$ is the constant of integration, then
questions.solution: Let $I=\int \frac{1}{x\left[(\log x)^2+4 \log x-1\right]} d x\begin{aligned} & =A \log \left[\frac{\log x+B}{\log x+C}\right]+K \\ & \text{ let } \log x=t \Rightarrow \frac{1}{x} d x=d t \\ & I=\int \frac{1}{t^2+4 t-1} d t=\int \frac{d t}{(t+2)^2-(\sqrt{5})^2} \\ & =\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{5}} \log \left[\frac{\log x+2-\sqrt{5}}{\log x+2+\sqrt{5}}\right] \\ & \Rightarrow A=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{5}}, B=2-\sqrt{5}, C=2+\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\frac{2 x^2+5 x+6}{(x+2)^3}=\frac{a}{x+2}+\frac{b}{(x+2)^2}+\frac{c}{(x+2)^3}$ then $\mathrm{a} . \mathrm{b}+\mathrm{b} . \mathrm{c}+\mathrm{c} . \mathrm{a}=$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} \text{ Given } \frac{2 x^2+5 x+6}{(x+2)^3}=\frac{a}{(x+2)}+\frac{b}{(x+2)^2}+\frac{c}{(x+3)^3}\\ \text{$ and $} \Rightarrow 2 x²+5 x+6=a(x+2)^2+b(x+2)+c \\ \text{ and } \Rightarrow 2 x²+5 x+6=x²(a)+x(4 a+b)+(4 a+2 b+c)
\end{aligned} Comparing we get, a=2, b=-3, c=4 Hence a \cdot$ b+b $\cdot$ c+c $\cdot$ a=-10

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\int\left(\frac{4 e^x+6 e^{-x}}{9 e^x-4 e^{-x}}\right) d x=A x+B \log \left|\left(9 e^{2 x}-4\right)\right|+C$, then $(\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B})=$
questions.solution: Let $I=\int \frac{4 e^x+6 e^{-x}}{9 e^x-4 e^{-x}} d x=\int \frac{4 e^{2 x}+6}{9 e^{2 x}-4} d x$ Let $4 e^{2 x}+6=A\left(9 e^{2 x}-4\right)+B\left(18 e^{2 x}\right)^{4} e^{2 x}+6=(9 A+18 B) e^{2 x}-4 A$ Comparing both sides we get, $A=-\frac{3}{2}, B=\frac{35}{36}\begin{aligned} & \therefore I=-\frac{3}{2} \int \frac{\left(9 e^{2 x}-4\right) d x}{\left(9 e^{2 x}-4\right)}+\frac{35}{36} \int \frac{18 e^{2 x}}{9 e^{2 x}-4} d x \\ & \Rightarrow \quad I=-\frac{3}{2} \int d x+\frac{35}{36} \int \frac{18 e^{2 x}}{9 e^{2 x}-4} d x \\ & \Rightarrow \quad I=-\frac{3}{2}+\frac{35}{36} \log \left|\left(9 e^{2 x}-4\right)\right|+c \\ & \text{ Hence } A=-\frac{3}{2}, \quad B=\frac{35}{36}\end{aligned}$

$\quad f(x)=\int \frac{d x}{x^2+(\sqrt{2})^2}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{2}}\right)+c$ Since at $x=\sqrt{2}, f(x)=0$
\Rightarrow 0=$\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \tan ^{-1}(1)+c \Rightarrow c=-\frac{\pi}{4 \sqrt{2}}$ Hence f(0)=$\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{0}{\sqrt{2}}\right)+\left(-\frac{\pi}{4 \sqrt{2}}\right)=-\frac{\pi}{4 \sqrt{2}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $I=\int_{-a}^a\left(x^4-2 x^2\right) d x$, then $I$ is minimum at $a=$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}& I=\int_{-a}^a\left( x^4-2 x²\right) d x \\
& \frac{d I}{d a}=\frac{d}{d a}\left[\int_{-a}^ a\left( x^4-2 x²\right) d x\right] \\
& =2 a⁴-4 a² \\
& \text{$ and $} \frac{d^2 I}{d a^2}=8 a³-8 a
\end{aligned} For minima, \frac{d I}{d \alpha}=0$
\Rightarrow a=0, $\pm \sqrt{2}$ but when $c=\sqrt{2}$ then $\frac{d^2 I}{d a^2}=8 \sqrt{2} > 0$
Hence $a=\sqrt{2}$ is minima

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Assertion (A): $\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{3}} \frac{(\sin x)^{\sqrt{2}} d x}{(\sin x)^{\sqrt{2}}+(\cos x)^{\sqrt{2}}}=\frac{\pi}{12}$
Reason (R): $\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{3}} \frac{f(x) d x}{f(x)+f\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}=\frac{\pi}{12}$
options: A is true, $\mathrm{R}$ is true and $\mathrm{R}$ is the correct explanation of A
A is true, $\mathrm{R}$ is true but $\mathrm{R}$ is not the correct explanation of $\mathrm{A}$
questions.solution:
Let $\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{(\sin x)^{\sqrt{2}} d x}{(\sin x)^{\sqrt{2}}+(\cos x)^{\sqrt{2}}}...(1)$
Since $\int_a^b f(x) d x=\int_a^b f(a+b-x) d x$
Hence $I=\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{(\cos x)^{\sqrt{2}} \cdot d x}{(\sin x)^{\sqrt{2}}+(\cos x)^{\sqrt{2}}}...(2) \begin{aligned}& \text{ Equation (1)+(2), }\\
& \Rightarrow I \int_{1 / 3}^{/ 3} \frac{(\sin x)^{\sqrt{2}}(\cos x)^{\sqrt{2}}}{(\sin x)^{\sqrt{2}}(\cos x)^{\sqrt{2}}} d x \\
& \Rightarrow I=\frac{\pi}{12}
\end{aligned}$ Hence Assertion ' A$ ' is correct. \begin{aligned}& \text{ Let } P=\int_{\pi/ 6}^{\pi/ 3} \frac{f(x) d x}{f(x)+f\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}...(3) \\
& \Rightarrow P=\int_{\pi/ 6}^{\pi/ 3} \frac{f\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right) d x}{f(x)+f\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}...(4)
\end{aligned} Equation (3) + (4), 2 P=\int_{\pi/ 6}^{\pi/ 3} d x \Rightarrow P=\frac{\pi}{12}$ Hence Reason $R$ is also true putting $f(x)=(\sin x)^{\sqrt{2}}$ in Reason ' $R$ ' we get$\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{(\sin x)^{\sqrt{2}} d x}{(\sin x)^{\sqrt{2}}+(\cos x)^{\sqrt{2}}}=\frac{\pi}{12}$
Hence $R$ is correct explanation of ' A$ '$

questions.q:
$\int \frac{3 e^x-7 e^{-x}}{7 e^x+3 e^{-x}} d x=K x+L \log \left(e^{-2 x}+\frac{7}{3}\right)+C$
then $K+L=$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} I & =\int \frac{3 e^x-7 e^{-x}}{7 e^x+3 e^{-x}} d x \\ & =3 \int \frac{e^x-\frac{7}{3} e^{-x}}{7 e^x+3 e^{-x}} d x \\ & =\frac{3}{7} \int \frac{7 e^x-\frac{49}{3} e^{-x}}{7 e^x+3 e^{-x}} d x \\ & =\frac{3}{7} \int \frac{\left(7 e^x+3 e^{-x}\right)-\frac{58}{3} e^{-x}}{7 e^x+3 e^{-x}} d x \\ & =\frac{3}{7} \int d x-\frac{3}{7} \times \frac{58}{3} \int \frac{e^{-x}}{7 e^x+3 e^{-x}} d x\end{aligned}I=\frac{3 x}{7}-\frac{58}{7} \int \frac{e^{-2 x}}{7+3 e^{-2 x}} d x$
Put $t=7+3 e^{-2 x}\Rightarrow \quad d t=-6 e^{-2 x} d x\begin{aligned} & I=\frac{3 x}{7}-\frac{58}{7}\left(-\frac{1}{6}\right) \int \frac{d t}{t} \\ & I=\frac{3 x}{7}+\frac{29}{21} \ln |t|+C \\ & I=\frac{3 x}{7}+\frac{29}{21} \ln \left(7+3 e^{-2 x}\right)+C\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad K=3 / 7 \text{$ and $} L=29 / 21 \\ & \Rightarrow K+L=\frac{3}{7}+\frac{29}{21}=\frac{9+29}{21}=\frac{38}{21}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int(\sqrt{x+\sqrt{12 x-36}}+\sqrt{x-\sqrt{12 x-36}}) d x=$
questions.solution:
$I=\int(\sqrt{x+\sqrt{12 x-36}}+\sqrt{x-\sqrt{12 x-36}} d x$
Put $t^2=12 x-36\Rightarrow x=\frac{t^2+36}{12}$ and $2 t d t=12 d x \Rightarrow t d t=6 d xI=\int\left(\sqrt{\frac{t^2+36}{12}+t}+\sqrt{\frac{t^2+36}{12}-t}\right)\left(\frac{t}{6}\right) d tI=\frac{1}{6} \int \frac{\{(t+6)+(t-6)\}}{\sqrt{12}} t d t \quad\left[\right.$ when $\left.t^2 > 36\right]\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{6 \sqrt{12}} \int(2 t) t d t=\frac{1}{3 \sqrt{12}} \int t^2 d t \\ & =\frac{1}{3 \sqrt{12}}\left(\frac{t^3}{3}\right)+C=\frac{1}{9 \sqrt{12}}(12 x-36)^{\frac{3}{2}}+C \\ & =\frac{(1.2)^{3 / 2}}{9(12)^{1 / 2}}(x-3)^{3 / 2}+C=\frac{12}{9}(x-3)^{3 / 2}+C \\ & =\frac{4}{3}(x-3)^{3 / 2}+C, \text{ if } x > 6\end{aligned}$
Now, $I=\frac{1}{6 \sqrt{12}} \int\{t+6-(t-6)\} t d t[3 \leq x \leq 6]\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{6 \sqrt{12}} \int 12 t d t=\frac{\sqrt{12}}{6} \int t d t \\ & =\frac{\sqrt{12}}{6}\left(\frac{t^2}{2}\right)+C^{\prime}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{12}}(12 x-36)+C^{\prime} \\ & =\sqrt{12} x+\left(\frac{-36}{\sqrt{12}}+C^{\prime}\right)\end{aligned}\therefore \quad I=2 \sqrt{3} x+C$, if $3 \leq x \leq 6$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\begin{aligned} & \int \frac{x d x}{\sqrt[15]{\left(1+x^2\right)^{12}\left(2+x^2\right)^{18}}}=\alpha\left(\frac{1+x^2}{2+x^2}\right)^{1 / n}+C \Rightarrow \\ & \frac{n}{\alpha}=\end{aligned}$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} I & =\int \frac{x d x}{\sqrt[15]{\left(1+x^2\right)^{12}\left(2+x^2\right)^{18}}} \\ & =\int \frac{x d x}{\left(1+x^2\right)^{12 / 15}\left(2+x^2\right)^{18 / 15}} \\ & =\int \frac{x d x}{\left(1+x^2\right)^{4 / 5}\left(2+x^2\right)^{6 / 5}} \\ & =\int \frac{x d x}{\left(1+x^2\right)^2\left(\frac{2+x^2}{1+x^2}\right)^{6 / 5}}\end{aligned}$
Put $u=\frac{2+x^2}{1+x^2}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad d u=\left\{\frac{\left(1+x^2\right)(2 x)-\left(2+x^2\right)(2 x)}{\left(1+x^2\right)^2}\right\} d x \\ & \Rightarrow d u=\frac{2 x\left(1+x^2-2-x^2\right) d x}{\left(1+x^2\right)^2} \\ & \Rightarrow d u=\frac{-2 x d x}{\left(1+x^2\right)^2} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{x d x}{\left(1+x^2\right)^2}=-\frac{d u}{2}\end{aligned}$
Then, $I=-\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{d x}{(u)^{6 / 5}}\begin{aligned} & =-\frac{1}{2}\left\{\frac{u^{\frac{-6}{5}}+1}{\left(-\frac{6}{5}+1\right)}\right\}+C \\ & =\frac{5}{2} \times(u)^{-1 / 5}+C \\ & =\frac{5}{2}\left(\frac{1+x^2}{2+x^2}\right)^{1 / 5}+C\end{aligned}$
Thus, $\alpha=\frac{5}{2}$ and n=5
Then, $\frac{n}{\alpha}=\frac{5}{5 / 2}=2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int(\log x)^2 x^3 d x=\frac{x^4}{32} f(x)+C \Rightarrow f(x)=$
questions.solution:
$I=\int(\log x)^2 x^3 d x$
Using integration by parts,
$I=(\log x)^2 \int x^3 d x-\int\left(\frac{d(\log x)^2}{d x} \int x^3 d x\right) d x\begin{aligned} & =\frac{(\log x)^2 x^4}{4}-\int \frac{2 \log x}{x} \times \frac{x^4}{4} d x \\ & \quad=\frac{(\log x)^2 x^4}{4}-\frac{1}{2} \int(\log x) x^3 d x \\ & \quad=\frac{(\log x)^2 x^4}{4}-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}\left[(\log x) \int x^3 d x-\int\left(\frac{d \log x}{d x} \int x^3 d x\right) d x\right]\begin{aligned} & =\frac{(\log x)^2 x^4}{4}-\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{(\log x) x^4}{4}-\int \frac{1}{x} \times \frac{x^4}{4} d x\right] \\ & =\frac{(\log x)^2 x^4}{4}-\frac{1}{8}(\log x) x^4+\frac{1}{8} \times \frac{x^4}{4}+C \\ & =\frac{x^4}{32}\left[8(\log x)^2-4(\log x)+1\right]+C\end{aligned}\therefore f(x)=8(\log x)^2-4(\log x)+1$
